TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r1.claim: Exalting God from what is unfit prepares for knowledge of His perfection; this passage names that prerequisite because it describes qualities leading believers to His light.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r1.anchor: والآية في مقام بيان خصالهم التي تستدعي هدايتهم إلى نوره فلا جرم اقتصر فيها بذكر ما هي المقدمة وهو التسبيح

TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r2.claim: Commerce denotes sustained earning through buying and selling, while a sale is a discrete transaction; together the negations cover continuous and occasional distraction from God.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r2.anchor: التجارة إذا قوبلت بالبيع كان المفهوم منها بحسب العرف الاستمرار في الاكتساب بالبيع والشراء والبيع هو العمل الاكتسابي الدفعي

TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r3.claim: An alternative says profitable sales are negated separately because their immediate gain can distract even when the trade as a profession does not.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r3.anchor: وقيل الوجه في نفي البيع بعد نفي إلهاء التجارة أن الربح في البيع ناجز بالفعل

TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabataba'i calls the explanation for separately negating sale a good one; repeating the negative particle reinforces the denial.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r4.anchor: لتذكير النفي وتأكيده، وهو وجه حسن

TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r5.claim: The form iqām is a shortened form of iqāma, with the tāʾ omitted for ease of pronunciation.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r5.anchor: الإقام هو الإقامة بحذف التاء تخفيفا

TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r6.claim: Establishing prayer and giving zakat represent all commanded good works; prayer stands for duties toward God and zakat for duties toward creation, each being a central pillar.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بإقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة الإتيان بجميع الأعمال الصالحة التي كلف الله تعالى عباده بإتيانها في حياتهم الدنيا

TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r7.claim: Because prayer and zakat are also remembrance, their contrast with remembrance points to inward, knowing remembrance of God, opposite forgetfulness and heedlessness.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r7.anchor: والمقابلة بين ذكر الله وبين إقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وهما - وخاصة الصلاة - من ذكر الله

TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r8.claim: The verse pairs sustained commerce and individual sales with constant inward remembrance and time-bound acts of worship: neither kind of distraction diverts them.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r8.anchor: لا يشتغلون بشيء عن ذكرهم المستمر بقلوبهم لربهم وذكرهم الموقت بأعمالهم من الصلاة والزكاة

TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r9.claim: The feared day is Resurrection, and the definite plural hearts and eyes includes those of both believers and disbelievers.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#2/r9.anchor: والمراد بالقلوب والأبصار ما يعم قلوب المؤمنين والكافرين وأبصارهم لكون القلوب والأبصار جمعا محلى باللام

TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r1.claim: At Resurrection, worldly perception that distracts from God and veils truth gives way to perception through faith and knowledge; believers see God's generosity, while disbelievers are blind and meet what pains them.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r1.anchor: فتنصرف القلوب والأبصار يومئذ عن المشاهدة والرؤية الدنيوية الشاغلة عن الله الساترة للحق والحقيقة

TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r2.claim: This description is singled out because the passage concerns the means by which God guides people to the faith and knowledge that will illuminate their sight in the next life.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r2.anchor: أن الكلام مسوق لبيان ما يتوسل به إلى هدايته تعالى إلى نوره وهو نور الإيمان والمعرفة

TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r3.claim: He interprets hearts and eyes here as souls and their inner insights.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r3.anchor: أن المراد بالقلوب والأبصار النفوس وبصائرها

TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r4.claim: The turning of perception explains their fear: one outcome is permanent deprivation of God's light and honor, ending in lasting misery and punishment; ultimately they fear themselves.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#3/r4.anchor: يخافون هذا التقلب لما في أحد شقيه من الحرمان من نور الله والنظر إلى كرامته

TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r6.claim: The Prophet and his purified household are among the finest applications of the verse; its apparent scope includes other prophets, successors, and saints, but not every believer because its described qualities are not universal.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#9/r6.anchor: فالآية تعم بظاهرها غيرهم من الأنبياء عليهم السلام والأوصياء والأولياء

TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r5.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r5.claim: In a Nahj al-Balagha sermon, Ali describes people of remembrance who trade the world for remembrance, warn the heedless, enjoin justice, and forbid wrong.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r5.anchor: وفي نهج البلاغة من كلام له عليه السلام عند تلاوته

TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r6.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r6.claim: Ali portrays them as living in this world as if already in the next, aware of barzakh and resurrection and revealing what ordinary people cannot see or hear.
TABATABAI:24:35-46#10/r6.anchor: كأنما قطعوا الدنيا إلى الآخرة وهم فيها فشاهدوا ما وراء ذلك

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r4.claim: The parable contrasts believers, whose hearts shine inwardly and outwardly, with unbelievers, surrounded by darkness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r4.anchor: hearts which have faith in them shine both inwardly and outwardly.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتههاءالتأنيثعوضالما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتههاءالتأنيثعوضالما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتههاءالتأنيثعوضالما.claim: Feminine tāʾ can compensate for a deleted final weak letter in verbal nouns, as in إقامة, استعانة and إراءة; the verse has إقامة الصلاة and إيتاء الزكاة.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتههاءالتأنيثعوضالما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتههاءالتأنيثعوضالما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتههاءالتأنيثعوضالما.claim: When the full form is retained, compensation may be omitted: اختيار has no feminine tāʾ, and إراءة also occurs as إراء, parallel to إقاما.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتههاءالتأنيثعوضالما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتههاءالتأنيثعوضالما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتههاءالتأنيثعوضالما.claim: Deletion is unavailable in تعزية and similar forms; تجزئة and تهنئة retain their forms by analogy with derived forms, just as أرأيت was reshaped as أريت after أقمت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتههاءالتأنيثعوضالما.anchor: وأما عزيت تعزية ونحوها فلا يجوز الحذف فيه

SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r2.claim: On the passive reading, rijāl may be nominative after an omitted verb answering an implied question, Who glorifies Him? Al-Samīn cites a poetic line with ḍāriʿ as such an answer, while noting disagreement over this construction.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r2.anchor: كأنه قيل: من يبكيه؟ فقيل: يبكيه ضارع

SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r3.claim: The second parse makes rijāl the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning those who glorify Him are men; this reading allows a pause at al-āṣāl.
SAMIN-DURR:24:36#2/r3.anchor: والوجه الثاني في البيت: أن " يزيد " منادى

SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r1.claim: The clause lā tulhīhim is a nominative adjective describing rijāl.
SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r1.anchor: في محل رفع صفة ل " رجال "

SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r2.claim: Yakhāfūn may be a second adjective of rijāl or a circumstantial clause describing the object of tulhīhim.
SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r2.anchor: يجوز أن تكون نعتا ثانيا لرجال، وأن تكون حالا من مفعول

SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r3.claim: On the stronger parse, yawman is a direct object rather than an adverb, and yataqallabu is an adjective of that day.
SAMIN-DURR:24:37/r3.anchor: و " يوما " مفعول به لا ظرف على الأظهر

ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r8.claim: Commerce and sale do not distract these men from God's remembrance, prayer, and almsgiving; nothing occupies them away from these duties.
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r8.anchor: ومعنى: (لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة). أي لا يشغلهم أمر عن ذلك.

ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd saw marketplace people leave their business and go to prayer when it was called, and identified them with this verse's men.
ZAJJAJ:v4p45/r9.anchor: ويروى أن ابن مسعود رأى قوما من أهل السوق، وقد نودي بالصلاة فتركوا بياعاتهم ونهضوا إلى الصلاة،

ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r1.claim: إقامة derives from أقمت إقواما; the wāw changes, one of the resulting alifs drops, tāʾ compensates for the deletion, and annexation here serves in place of the omitted tāʾ. Grammarians agree.
ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r1.anchor: الكلام أقمت الصلاة إقامة، وأصلها أقمت إقواما، ولكن قلبت الواو أيضا فاجتمعت ألفان، فحذفت إحداهما لالتقاء الساكنين،

ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r2.claim: Although تقلب is valid Arabic, it is not a Qur'anic reading because recitation is transmitted and must not be altered.
ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r2.anchor: ويجوز تقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار، في غير القرآن، ولا يجوز في القران " تقلب، لأن القراءة سنة لا تخالف

ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r3.claim: The hearts and eyes tremble and dry from distress and fear; the resurrection believer gains insight and sees the promised good, while others learn its reality through heart and sight.
ZAJJAJ:v4p46/r3.anchor: ومعنى تتقلب أي ترجف وتجف من الجزع والخوف، ومعناه أن من كان قلبه موقنا بالبعث والقيامة ازداد بصيرة،

ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n57/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n57/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n57/r1.claim: Bayʿ literally means bargaining, selling, or buying and selling, and stands for anything that might bring worldly gain.
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n57/r1.anchor: Lit., "bargaining" or "selling" or "buying and selling" (bay') - a metonym for anything that might bring worldly gain.

ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n58/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n58/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n58/r1.claim: For his rendering of zakah, Asad refers readers to surah 2, note 34.
ASAD-NOTES:24:36#n58/r1.anchor: For this rendering of the term zakah, see surah 2, note 34.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p1/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p1/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p1/r1.claim: Qur'anic expression is deliberate: every word and letter is intentionally placed.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p1/r1.anchor: القرآن هو تعبير بياني مقصود أي أن كل كلمة وكل حرف فيه وُضع وضعاً مقصوداً

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p1/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p1/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p1/r4.claim: The phrase فيه is included because this day is specifically the Day of Resurrection and reckoning.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p1/r4.anchor: اليوم منحصر في يوم القيامة والحساب لذا ذكر (فيه)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p452/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p452/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p452/r1.claim: Omitting فيه with the reward wording in 31:33 generalizes its effect beyond that day; it is retained in 2:281 and 24:37 because those refer specifically to the Day of Judgment.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p452/r1.anchor: الحذف يفيد الإطلاق ولا يختص بذلك اليوم. فالجزاء ليس منحصراً في ذلك اليوم وإنما سيمتد أثره إلى ما بعد ذلك اليوم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r2.claim: After the faith parable names mosques, the discourse describes how believers live; it states the effect after its cause so faith is personified in lived conduct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r2.anchor: This is like stating the effect after stating the cause so that a fact can be personified in real life.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r4.claim: The indefinite noun رجال intensifies praise: these are superb servants whom worldly things cannot distract from remembering God, whose pleasure they cherish most.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r4.anchor: is meant for extreme praise of such people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r5.claim: Tijārah means trade generally, while bayʿ conventionally means selling; the wording names a specific activity after the general term.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r5.anchor: conventionally means “to sell.” This is a mention of the specific after the general.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r6.claim: Even highly profitable chances to sell do not distract these believers from God's remembrance; they conduct business without neglecting remembrance or their obligations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r6.anchor: A businessman never loses the opportunity to sell his goods if the occasion arises; however, such are these servants of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r7.claim: Prayer and zakāh are the two basic religious duties and in reality encompass the whole religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r7.anchor: The prayer and zakāh are mentioned as two basic obligations of religion. In reality, they encompass the whole of religion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r8.claim: The image of hearts and eyes turning over depicts Judgment Day's horrors, when people who lived heedlessly remain anxious and dismayed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p334/r8.anchor: portray the horrors of the Day of Judgement.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r4.claim: Ibn Umar said the verse was revealed about people who closed their shops when prayer was called and entered the mosque.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p60#3/r4.anchor: عن سالم عن ابن عمر أنه كان في السوق فأقيمت الصلاة فأغلقوا حوانيتهم فدخلوا المسجد فقال ابن عمر فيهم نزلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r1.claim: The worshippers maintain prayer and give zakāt while fearing what comes at resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r1.anchor: وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وخوفهم ما يكون في البعث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r2.claim: The passage contrasts believers affected by kinds of guidance with disbelievers who cannot receive it, following the mention of guidance to the light.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48/r2.anchor: ولذلك جاء مقابل المؤمنين وهم الكفار في قوله والذين كفروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r4.claim: On the two passive readings, rijāl may be the agent of an omitted verb, yusabbiḥu or yusabbaḥu lahum; alternatively it is the predicate of an omitted subject, al-musabbiḥ rijāl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r4.anchor: وارتفع رجال على هاتين القراءتين على الفاعلية بإضمار فعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r5.claim: One syntactic analysis allows a construction like ḍuribat Hind Zayd, while another makes rijāl a predicate of an omitted subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r5.anchor: فعلى اقتياسه نحو ضربت هند زيد أي ضربها زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r6.claim: One possibility is that the men have no trade or sales at all that could distract them, like a road with no beacon to guide travelers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r6.anchor: أحدهما: أنهم لا تجارة لهم ولا بيع فيلهيهم عن ذكر الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r7.claim: The other possibility is that they do trade and sell but are not distracted from God's remembrance or their obligations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r7.anchor: والثاني: أنهم ذوو تجارة وبيع ولكن لا يشغلهم ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r8.claim: The apparent coordination distinguishes trade from sale; trade may mean buying paired with sale, or caravan commerce paired with market sales.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r8.anchor: والظاهر مغايرة التجارة والبيع، ولذلك عطف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, sale is a specific kind after the general term trade, which includes buying and selling to seek profit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r9.anchor: لأن التجارة هي البيع والشراء طلبا للربح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r10.claim: Sale is singled out because an imminent profitable deal is more distracting than a hoped-for gain: the former is certain and the latter only expected.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r10.anchor: ونبه على هذا الخاص لأنه في الإلهاء أدخل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the tāʾ in iqāma replaces the lost root consonant; the original was iqwām, and annexation removes the compensating tāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p48#2/r11.anchor: قال الزمخشري: التاء في إقامة عوض من العين الساقطة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r1.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ holds that the tāʾ drops because of annexation; the Basrans hold that it does not drop for that reason.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r1.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكر من أن التاء سقطت لأجل الإضافة هو مذهب الفراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r2.speaker: خالد بن كلثوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r2.claim: Khālid b. Kulthūm interprets ʿadā al-amr in the cited poem as the plural of ʿidwa, meaning the sides or aspects of a matter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r2.anchor: وقد تأول خالد بن كلثوم قوله عدا الأمر على أنه جمع عدوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r3.claim: The day they fear is the Day of Resurrection.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r4.claim: The hearts and eyes are shaken by the terror of that day, shifting from hope of salvation to hope and from fear of ruin to ruin; the state is like that in 33:10.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن معنى تتقلب تضطرب من هول ذلك اليوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r5.claim: The Arabs also use this kind of turning for the turmoil of battle, as in a cited line likening the heart to a bird's wings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r5.anchor: وهذا المعنى تستعمله العرب في الحروب كقوله:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r6.claim: The gloss that hearts turn on Hell's embers is remote because that occurs after the Day of Resurrection, not on it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r6.anchor: ويبعد قول من قال تتقلب على جمر جهنم لأن ذلك ليس في يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r7.claim: Another interpretation says hearts and eyes turn from false beliefs to the revealed truth, understanding and seeing after being sealed and blind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r7.anchor: وقول من قال إن تقلبها ظهور الحق لها أي فتتقلب عن معتقدات الضلال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the first interpretation as more forceful in magnifying the day's terror.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r9.speaker: ابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r9.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin assimilates the tāʾ in ta-taqallabu into the following tāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن: تقلب بإدغام التاء في التاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r12.claim: Yakhāfūna is an adjective describing rijāl, as lā tulhīhim is.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p49/r12.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله يخافون صفة لرجال كما أن لا تلهيهم كذلك.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r1.claim: The prepositional phrase في بيوت attaches to يسبح; its repetition as فيها emphasizes and recalls what follows, and fronting signals importance rather than restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r1.anchor: بيسبح وفيها تكرير لذلك جيء به للتأكيد والتذكير بما بعد في الجملة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r2.claim: Some grammarians call the repeated phrase بدل; al-Mughni calls it emphasis of the preposition by repeating it with an attached pronoun. Al-Alusi objects that explicit wording is stronger and cannot be emphasized by a pronoun; some allow بدل by analogy, and he answers that the whole phrase may be بدل or emphasis with an explicit form to avoid repetition.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r2.anchor: وبعض النحاة أعرب نحو ذلك بدلا كما في شرح التسهيل وفي المغنى هو من توكيد الحرف بإعادة ما دخل عليه مضمرا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r3.claim: رجال is the subject of يسبح and follows the circumstantial phrase because its lengthy description would disrupt the verse's smooth order if placed earlier.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p173#2/r3.anchor: رجال ( الخ استئناف لبيان حال من حصلت لهم الهداية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r9.claim: On the masculine passive reading, rijāl is raised either as the subject of an omitted verb or as the predicate of an omitted subject, supplying the men who glorify God.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r9.anchor: ورفع ( رجال ) على هذه القراءة على أنه فاعل لفعل محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r12.claim: A poetic example illustrates the accepted ellipsis of a verb or subject in this construction; many grammarians allow such ellipsis by analogy, unlike the explicitly disallowed use of an agent as a specification after a passive verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p176/r12.anchor: وهذا نظير قوله : لبيك يزيد ضارع لخصومة ومختبط مما تطيح الطوائح

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r1.claim: The clause describing what does not distract them qualifies rijāl and reinforces the grandeur conveyed by its indefinite form, emphasizing their unbroken devotion despite every possible diversion.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r1.anchor: وقوله سبحانه : ( لا تلهيهم تجارة ( صفة له مؤكدة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r2.claim: On the reading discussed above, rijāl is raised as subject or predicate; its tanwin in every reading conveys magnificence.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r2.anchor: فرفع ( رجال ) على هذه القراءة على الفاعلية أو الخبرية كما سمعت آنفا والتنوين فيه على جميع القراءات للتفخيم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r3.claim: Men are specified because they are especially suited to frequent mosques; a report from Umm Salama says women’s best mosques are the innermost parts of their homes.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r3.anchor: وتخصيص الرجال بالذكر لأنهم الأحقاء بالمساجد فقد أخرج أحمد والبيهقي عن أم سلمة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خير مساجد النساء

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r4.claim: Trade means exchange generally, while sale is one particular kind; sale is singled out because its profit is immediate and certain, unlike the uncertain future gain of other trade, so negating trade alone would not clearly negate its distraction.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r4.anchor: وتخصيص التجارة التي هي المعارضة مطلقا بذلك لكونها أقوى الصوارف عندهم وأشهرها أي لا يشغلهم نوع من أنواع التجارة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r5.claim: Repeating lā after trade emphasizes the negation; alternatively trade may mean profitable exchange and sale all exchange generally, making the second phrase a generalization after specification.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r5.anchor: وإفراده بالذكر اندراجه تحت التجارة للإيذان بإنافته على سائر أنواعها لأن ربحه متيقن ناجز وربح ما عداه متوقع

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r6.speaker: الواقدي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r6.claim: Al-Waqidi says trade here means buying, its origin and starting point, which removes the need to construe trade and sale as different categories.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r6.anchor: ونقل عن الواقدي أن المراد بالتجارة هو الشراء لأنه أصلها ومبدؤها فلا تخصيص ولا تعميم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r7.claim: Another explanation takes trade as importing goods, since bringing them in is customary to it; a report describing the men as traveling the earth to seek God’s bounty supports this.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r7.anchor: بالتجارة الجلب لأنه الغالب فيها فهو لازم لها عادة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r8.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says the men described in the verse travel the land seeking God’s bounty; al-Dailami transmits a similar report from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r8.anchor: ويؤيد هذا ما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says they really were merchants, yet trade and sale never distracted them from remembrance; al-Dahhak shares this view, which al-Alusi regards as supported by the verse’s apparent wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r9.anchor: وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس + أخرج الطبراني وابن مردويه عنه أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r10.claim: An alternative says the men had no trade or sale, so neither distracted them, and identifies them as people disengaged from worldly life such as the People of the Bench; al-Alusi prefers the merchant reading and says no reliable or weak report establishes this occasion.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p177/r10.anchor: وقيل : إنهم لم يكونوا تجارا والنفي راجع للقيد والمقيد

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r1.claim: Remembering God includes glorification, praise, and similar devotional acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r1.anchor: عن ذكر الله ( بالتسبيح والتحميد ونحوهما

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r2.claim: Establishing prayer means performing it at its appointed times without delay; the verbal noun iqāma is explained through deletion and vowel transfer from an original form.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r2.anchor: إقام الصلاة ( أي إقامتها لمواقيتها من غير تأخير

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r3.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains iqāma by changing wāw to alif and deleting an alif when two meet; al-Alusi objects that the change lacks its required condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r3.anchor: وعن الزجاج أنه قلبت الواو ألفا ثم حذف لاجتماع ألفين وأورد عليه أنه لا داعي إلى قلبها ألفا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r4.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r4.claim: Al-Farra permits deleting the final alif either with compensatory tāʾ, as in iqāma, or through annexation, as in this verse; Sībawayh permits deletion without either compensation.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r4.anchor: تعويض التاء فيقال : إقامة أو الإضافة كما هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r5.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r5.claim: Sībawayh allows the deletion without a compensatory tāʾ or annexation; the cited line is also explained by Khalid ibn Kulthum as using ʿadā for the plural of ʿadwa, meaning sides.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r5.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه جواز الحذف من غير تعويض التاء أو الإضافة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r6.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r6.claim: Al-Hasan interprets zakat here as the wealth mandated for distribution to eligible recipients, a reading supported by the phrase’s construction as giving zakat.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r6.anchor: أي المال الذي فرض إخراجه للمستحقين كما روي عن الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets giving zakat as sincere obedience to God, but al-Alusi considers this interpretation remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما تفسير إيتاء الزكاة بإخلاص طاعة الله تعالى وفيه بعد كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r8.claim: Zakat is mentioned even though it is not performed in mosques because it commonly accompanies prayer and shows that the men’s good deeds are not limited to what they do in mosques.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r8.anchor: وإيراد هذا الفعل ههنا وإن لم يكن مما يفعل في البيوت لكونه قرينة لا تفارق إقامة الصلاة في عامة المواضع

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r9.claim: The fear clause can further describe the men, be circumstantial to the object of “distract,” or stand independently as its explanation; in any case their fear is not confined to mosque settings.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178/r9.anchor: صفة أخرى لرجال أو حال من مفعول ( لا تلهيهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r1.claim: Yawm is the object of “they fear,” with an implied “punishment” or “terror” if supplied; making it a time adverb with an omitted object is remote, and making it an adverb of fear is untenable because they fear in this life.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r1.anchor: يوما ( مفعول ليخافون على تقدير مضاف أي عقاب يوم وهوله أو بدونه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r2.claim: The day is Judgment Day; the turning of hearts and eyes can mean that they themselves are convulsed and changed by terror, as in the description of the Confederates’ distress.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r2.anchor: والمراد به يوم القيامة ومعنى تقلب القلوب والأبصار فيه اضطرابها وتغيرها أنفسها فيه من الهول والفزع

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r3.claim: Other explanations are that hearts understand what they did not and eyes see what they did not, or that hearts alternate between hope and fear while eyes look in every direction as people await their fate and books.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r3.anchor: أو تغير أحوالها بأن تفقه القلوب ما لم تكن تفقه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r4.claim: The claim that hearts and eyes turn over the embers of Hell, and al-Jubbaʾi’s account of successive fiery states, are rejected as unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r4.anchor: ومثله قول الجبائي : أن المراد تنقل من حال إلى حال

ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r5.speaker: ابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r5.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads the second tāʾ of tattaqalabu with sukūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p178#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن ( تتقلب ) بإسكان التاء الثانية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r1.claim: Men are singled out in connection with these mosques because Friday and congregational prayers in the mosque are not obligatory for women.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r1.anchor: قيل: خص الرجال بالذكر في هذه المساجد لأنه ليس على النساء جمعة ولا جماعة في المسجد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r2.claim: Trade is singled out because it is the greatest activity likely to distract a person from prayer and worship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r2.anchor: قيل خص التجارة بالذكر لأنها أعظم ما يشتغل به الإنسان عن الصلاة والطاعات

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r3.claim: Although tijara can mean buying and selling, here it means buying, since selling is named separately; the Quran also uses tijara for buying.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r3.anchor: وأراد بالتجارة الشراء وإن كان اسم التجارة يقع على البيع والشراء جميعا لأنه ذكر البيع بعد هذا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r4.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r4.claim: Al-Farra distinguishes trade as the activity of merchants bringing goods and sale as what a man sells directly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: التجارة لأهل الجلب والبيع ما باعه الرجل على يديه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r5.claim: Not being distracted from God's remembrance means continuing to attend the mosques to perform prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r5.anchor: {ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} عن حضور المساجد لإقامة الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r6.claim: Iqam is understood as li-iqamat, with the final ta omitted; إقامة prayer means performing it at its time, since prayer delayed beyond its time is not properly established.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r6.anchor: {وإقام} أي: لإقامة، {الصلاة} حذف الهاء وأراد أداءها في وقتها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r7.claim: Although remembrance already means the five daily prayers, prayer's establishment is repeated here to emphasize keeping their appointed times.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r7.anchor: وأعاد ذكر إقامة الصلاة مع أن المراد من ذكر الله الصلوات الخمس لأنه أراد بإقام الصلاة حفظ المواقيت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r8.claim: Salim reports that Ibn Umar saw people close their market stalls and enter the mosque when prayer was called, and Ibn Umar said this verse was revealed about them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51/r8.anchor: روى سالم عن ابن عمر أنه كان في السوق فأقيمت الصلاة فقام الناس وأغلقوا حوانيتهم فدخلوا المسجد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r1.claim: The zakat meant is the obligatory alms.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says that when zakat becomes due, believers do not withhold it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه: إذا حضر وقت أداء الزكاة لم يحبسوها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r3.claim: An alternate interpretation takes zakat to mean righteous works.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r4.claim: One view says hearts turn away from their worldly state of disbelief and eyes are opened from their coverings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r4.anchor: قيل: تتقلب القلوب عما كانت عليه في الدنيا من الشرك والكفر، وتنفتح الأبصار من الأغطية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r5.claim: Another view says hearts alternate between fear of destruction and hope of deliverance, while eyes turn about in terror, including over whether records come from the right or left.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: تتقلب القلوب بين الخوف والرجاء تخشى الهلاك وتطمع في النجاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r6.claim: A further view says hearts rise inside the chest to the throat and remain there, while eyes stare fixed from the terror and severity of the event.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p51#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: تتقلب القلوب في الجوف فترتفع إلى الحنجرة فلا تنزل ولا تخرج

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r1.claim: Their profitable business does not distract them from remembrance, prayer, or almsgiving.

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r2.claim: Sale may generalize after trade, or single out the more important half of commerce, where profit is realized, unlike hoped-for gain in buying.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r2.anchor: ولا بيع عن ذكر الله } مبالغة بالتعميم بعد التخصيص

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r3.claim: Some understand trade as buying, its origin; others as importing, the common form, as in usage for bringing goods.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد بالتجارة الشراء فإنه أصلها ومبدؤها

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r4.claim: The mention of commerce hints that these worshippers are merchants.

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r5.claim: In iqām, the genitive construction replaces the tāʾ compensating for a weak root letter lost through phonetic change; a cited line illustrates the form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r5.anchor: الإضافة من التاء المعوضة عن العين الساقطة بالإعلال

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r6.claim: Zakāh is what must be paid from property to its rightful recipients.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r6.anchor: ما يجب إخراجه من المال للمستحقين

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r7.claim: They fear the coming day even while engaged in remembrance and obedience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r7.anchor: مع ما هم عليه من الذكر والطاعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r8.claim: Hearts and eyes may shake from terror, or their capacities may turn to perceive what they had not perceived.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r8.anchor: تضطرب وتتغير من الهول، أو تتقلب أحوالها فتفقه القلوب

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r9.claim: Alternatively, hearts turn between hope of rescue and fear of ruin, while eyes search how they will be taken and receive their records.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:37/r9.anchor: مع توقع النجاة وخوف الهلاك والأبصار من أي ناحية يؤخذ بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r8.claim: Trade includes sales or other profitable dealings; sale is separately mentioned because people may sell possessions to meet necessities, and al-bayʿ can mean either acquiring by purchase or disposing by sale.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r8.anchor: والبيع يطلق بالاشتراك على التحصيل الذي هو الشرى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r9.claim: Neither kind of business distracts these men from God's remembrance, through prayer or otherwise; they remain in continual awareness and watchfulness of Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r9.anchor: فهم كل وقت في شهود ومراقبة لمن تعرف إليهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r10.claim: Prayer is named explicitly after remembrance to stress guarding its time and all its requirements, even the least adequate performance; the wording does not demand the highest degree of perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r10.anchor: أعادها بعد ذكرها بالتسبيح تصريحا بها تأكيدا لها وحثا على حفظ وقتها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r11.claim: Zakat is the purification and growth of bodies, complementing prayer's purification of spirits.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r12.claim: Although women's attendance at mosques is an established sunnah, specifying men here signals that women's prayer at home is better; the supporting reports follow in the next segment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p266/r12.anchor: مع أن حضور النساء المساجد سنة شهيرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r1.claim: Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Khuzayma report from Ibn Masʿūd that a woman's prayer in the more private part of her home is better; the source glosses al-mikhdaʿ as a storage closet. No grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r1.anchor: صلاة المرأة في بيتها أفضل من صلاتها في حجرتها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r2.speaker: أم سلمة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r2.claim: A report from Umm Salama, cited from Aḥmad, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn Khuzayma, and al-Ḥākim, says the best mosque for women is the innermost part of their homes. No grading is stated.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r3.speaker: أم حميدة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r3.claim: Umm Ḥumayd asked to pray with the Prophet; he said prayer at home was better, increasingly so from private room to house to local mosque to his mosque. She built a mosque in the darkest, farthest part of her home and prayed there until death.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r3.anchor: عن أم حميدة امرأة أبي حميد الساعدي رضي الله عنهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r4.claim: The feared day is the Resurrection, when the hearts and eyes turn between hope of salvation and fear of destruction because of its terror.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r4.anchor: وهو يوم القيامة , هو بحيث { تتقلب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p267/r5.claim: The two written tāʾs in tatqallabu emphasize the visible intensity of the hearts' and eyes' turning.

DURR-FULL:v6p202/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r5.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r5.claim: The Prophet says that at the gathering on Judgment Day a herald will call for the generous, those who left their beds for worship, those not distracted by trade, and those who praised God.
DURR-FULL:v6p202/r5.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: يجمع الناس في صعيد واحد ينفذهم البصر ويسمعهم الداعي

DURR-FULL:v6p206/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r3.claim: Umm Salama reports the Prophet's teaching that the best prayer places for women are the innermost parts of their homes.
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r3.anchor: عن أم سلمة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: خير مساجد النساء قعر بيوتهن

DURR-FULL:v6p206/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r4.claim: In response to women wanting to pray with him, the Prophet says their prayer at home is better than in their chambers, and prayer in their chambers better than in the congregation.
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r4.anchor: عن أبي حميد الساعدي عن أبيه عن جدته أم حميد قالت: قلت يا رسول الله تمنعنا أزواجنا أن نصلي معك

DURR-FULL:v6p206/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud says a woman's best prayer is at home, except at the Sacred Mosque; he also mentions an elderly woman in her later years.
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: ما صلت امرأة قط صلاة أفضل من صلاة تصليها في بيتها

DURR-FULL:v6p206/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r6.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r6.claim: The Prophet identifies the men not distracted by trade as people who travel the earth seeking God's bounty.
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله تعالى {رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} قال: هم الذين

DURR-FULL:v6p206/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r7.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r7.claim: Abu Saʿid reports the same Prophetic explanation: they are people who travel in search of God's bounty.
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r7.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله {رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} قال: هم الذين

DURR-FULL:v6p206/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says they sought God's bounty by buying and selling, but when they heard the call to prayer they left their goods and went to the mosque.
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} قال: كانوا رجالا يبتغون من فضل الله

DURR-FULL:v6p206/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r9.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas stresses that they were merchants, yet their trade never distracted them from remembering God.
DURR-FULL:v6p206/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} قال: أما والله ولقد كانوا تجارا

DURR-FULL:v6p207/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas connects the parable of God's light as a niche to these men, who were among the busiest traders yet were never distracted by business.
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: ضرب الله هذا المثل قوله {مثل نوره كمشكاة} لأولئك القوم الذين لا تلهيهم تجارة

DURR-FULL:v6p207/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “God's remembrance” here as attending the prescribed prayer; Ataa gives the same explanation.
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} قال: عن شهود الصلاة المكتوبة وأخرج الفريابي عن عطاء مثله

DURR-FULL:v6p207/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r3.claim: Ibn Umar saw people close their market shops when prayer was called and go to the mosque, and said the verse was revealed about them.
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r3.anchor:
عن ابن عمر:
انه كان في السوق فأقيمت الصلاة فأغلقوا حوانيتهم

DURR-FULL:v6p207/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud saw market sellers abandon their goods and rise for prayer when they heard the call, identifying them as the men described in the verse.
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه رأى ناسا من أهل السوق سمعوا الأذان فتركوا أمتعتهم

DURR-FULL:v6p207/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says their hearts turn within their bodies and cannot emerge until reaching the throats, like the description in Ghafir 40:18.
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r5.anchor: قال: تتقلب في الجوف ولا تقدر تخرج حتى تقع في الحنجرة

DURR-FULL:v6p207/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies the day they fear as Judgment Day.
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r6.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله {يخافون يوما} قال يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v6p207/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r7.claim: Abu al-Darda would like to earn three hundred dinars daily trading at the mosque steps and still attend congregational prayer, because he wants to be among the men described.
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r7.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: أحب أن أبايع على هذا الدرج وأربح كل يوم ثلثمائة دينار

DURR-FULL:v6p207/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r8.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r8.claim: Asma bint Yazid reports that on Judgment Day God will gather all people in one plain, where the caller can reach them and sight can see them.
DURR-FULL:v6p207/r8.anchor: عن أسماء بنت يزيد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجمع الله الناس يوم القيامة في صعيد واحد

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r1.claim: The Prophet says these are people who travel the land seeking God’s bounty.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله : رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله قال هم الذين يضربون في الارض

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās connects these men with the people described by the parable of God’s light: the lamp in its glass represents those whom trade does not distract.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : في بيوت اذن الله ان ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه يسبح له فيها بالغدو والاصال رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar saw people close their shops and go to the mosque when prayer was called, and said this verse was revealed about them.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر انه كان في السوق فاقيمت الصلاة فاغلقوا حوانيتهم ودخلوا المسجد فقال ابن عمر : فيهم نزلت

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r4.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r4.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says he could earn 300 dinars daily trading at the steps and still attend mosque prayer; although he regards this as lawful, he hopes to be among those described.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r4.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء : اني اقمت على هذا الدرج ابايع عليه اربح كل يوم ثلاثمائة دينار ، واشهد الصلاة في كل يوم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says they do buy and sell in the markets, but trade does not distract them from prayer when its time arrives.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2607/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك : رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله قال : هم في اسواقهم يبيعون ويشترون

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r1.speaker: سعيد بن أبي الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan describes people whose commerce does not keep them from attending prayer at its appointed time.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن أبي الحسن في قوله : رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله قال : قوم في تجارتهم وبيوعهم لا تلهيهم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r2.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r2.claim: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh points to the people he saw close their market stalls and go to the mosque for prayer as the men described.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r2.anchor: عن عمرو بن دينار الاعور ، قال : كنت مع سالم بن عبد الله ، ونحن نريد المسجد فمررنا بسوق المدينة وقد قاموا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r3.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says buying and selling did not distract them from fulfilling God’s obligatory rights at their appointed times.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r3.anchor: عن عطاء رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله واقام الصلاة قال : كانوا لا يلهيهم الشراء والبيع عن مواضع حقوق الله

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r4.speaker: مطر
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r4.claim: Maṭar says they traded, but when they heard the call to prayer, they put down even a scale in hand and went to prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r4.anchor: عن مطر في قول الله : رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله قال : اما انهم قد كانوا يشترون ويبيعون

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies remembrance of God as the obligatory prayer; the same is reported from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas and Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : عن ذكر الله يقول : عن الصلاة المكتوبة ، وروى عن الربيع بن انس ، ومقاتل بن حيان نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam glosses «establishing prayer» as establishing the religion.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r6.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم في قول الله : واقام الصلاة قال : اقامة الدين

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya explains the phrase as the obligatory prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2608/r7.anchor: عن أبي العالية ، قال : رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله واقام الصلاة يعني الصلاة المفروضة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says it means establishing the prayer in congregation.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r1.anchor: عن السدي قوله : واقام الصلاة قال : اقامة الصلاة في جماعة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r2.claim: Muqātil says they attended prayer and performed it as God commanded, preserving its times and what God entrusted to them.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r2.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان واقام الصلاة يعني : لا يلهيهم ذلك عن حضور الصلاة ان يقيموها كما امرهم الله

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses zakāt here as obedience to God and sincerity.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : الزكاة يعني بالزكاة طاعة الله والاخلاص

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r4.claim: When ʿAlqama and Masrūq both declined a drink because they were fasting, Ibn Masʿūd drank and recited that they fear the Day when hearts and eyes turn about.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r4.anchor: عن مسروق ، قال : اتى عبد الله بشراب فقال : اعط علقمة ، فقال : اني صائم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies the feared day as the Day of Resurrection.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r5.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم في قول الله : يخافون يوما تتقلب فيه القلوب والابصار قال : يوم القيامة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says hearts turn within the chest and cannot emerge until they reach the throat, as in the description of hearts at throats.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2609/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك قوله : يوما تتقلب فيه القلوب والابصار قال : تتقلب القلوب في الجوف ولا تقدر تخرج حتى تقع في الحنجرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r3.claim: On the monastic reading, these are monks who withdrew from worldly work; “no trade or sale distracts them” means they have no distracting commerce at all.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r3.anchor: وأريد بالرجال الذين لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله : الرهبان الذين انقطعوا للعبادة وتركوا الشغل بأمور الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r4.claim: The monks deserved praise because they then held sound faith: Islam had not reached them before Muslim conquests near Syria after Tabūk, and the Prophet's letter to Heraclius had not become public.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p246/r4.anchor: والثناء عليهم يومئذ لأنهم كانوا على إيمان صحيح إذ لم تبلغهم يومئذ دعوة الإسلام ولم تبلغهم إلا بفتوح مشارف الشام بعد غزوة تبوك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r4.claim: Another possible parse makes “in houses” the fronted predicate and “men” the subject, answering the implied question of who is guided to God's light in 24:35.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r4.anchor: ويجوز عندي أن يكون { في بيوت } خبرا مقدما و { رجال } مبتدأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r5.claim: On this reading, the men are the Companions and those like them; the houses include Muslim mosques and other prayer houses, including the Prophet's Mosque, Qubāʾ, and Juwāthā in Bahrain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r5.anchor: والرجال أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والبيوت مساجد المسلمين وغيرها من بيوت الصلاة في أرض الإسلام والمسجد النبوي ومسجد قباء بالمدينة ومسجد جؤاثى بالبحرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r8.claim: For this mosque reading, the men are the Prophet's Companions and others similarly devoted to mosques; men are singled out because they predominate in mosques, as in the report about one whose heart is attached to mosques.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r8.anchor: والمراد بالرجال : أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن كان مثلهم في التعلق بالمساجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p247/r9.claim: The Prophet describes among the seven shaded on the Day of Resurrection a man whose heart is attached to mosques.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r1.claim: Tijārah is acquiring goods to resell for profit; bayʿ is broader, covering a sale by anyone seeking its price.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r1.anchor: والتجارة : جلب السلع للربح في بيعها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r3.claim: For the passive reading, the “men” clause is resumed with an omitted verb prompted by yusabbiḥu, as in Nahshal ibn Ḥarrī's verse about a mourner weeping for Yazīd.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r3.anchor: على نحو قول نهشل بن حري يرثي أخاه يزيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r4.claim: The clauses about undistracted commerce and fearing the Day describe the men and implicitly contrast them with hypocrites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r4.anchor: وجملة : { لا تلهيهم تجارة } وجملة : { يخافون } صفتان ل { رجال }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r5.claim: Iqām is an ifʿāl verbal noun with a weak middle radical; it shifts and lengthens as expected, but unlike most such forms, it has no final tāʾ marbūṭah; see 2:3.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r5.anchor: و { إقام } مصدر على وزن الإفعال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r6.claim: Yawman is the object of “fear,” not a temporal adverb; the implied construction is “they fear the terrors of a day.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r6.anchor: وانتصب { يوما } من قوله : { يخافون يوما } على المفعول به لا على الظرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r7.claim: Hearts and eyes turn in fear and dread as a person tosses about in place; compare 6:110. Fear prompts action that leads to success on that Day, as 24:38 indicates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p249/r7.anchor: اضطرابها عن مواضعها من الخوف والوجل كما يتقلب المرء في مكانه

BURSEVI:v6p115/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115/r3.claim: Rijal is the subject of the verb yusabbihu.

BURSEVI:v6p115/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115/r4.claim: The phrase means nothing distracts them from their complete absorption in witnessing; the verb denotes diverting someone from what matters more.
BURSEVI:v6p115/r4.anchor: لا تشغلهم من غاية الاستغراق في مقام الشهود يقال : ألهاه عن كذا إذا شغله عما هو أهم

BURSEVI:v6p115/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115/r5.claim: Trade refers to buying and selling; al-Mufradat defines it as deploying capital in pursuit of profit. It is singled out as their strongest and most familiar distraction, meaning no kind of trade distracts them.
BURSEVI:v6p115/r5.anchor: تخصيص التجارة لكونها أقوى الصوارف عندهم وأشهرها أي لا يشغلهم نوع من أنواع التجارة

BURSEVI:v6p115/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115/r6.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p115/r6.claim: Al-Mufradat defines trade as managing capital to seek profit and notes this is the only Arabic word with ta followed by jim.
BURSEVI:v6p115/r6.anchor: المفردات" : التجارة التصرف في رأس المال طالبا للربح وليس في كلامهم تاء بعدها جيم

BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r1.claim: Sale is giving the merchandise and receiving its price; purchase is giving the price and receiving the merchandise.
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r1.anchor: البيع إعطاء المثمن وأخذ الثمن والشراء إعطاء الثمن وأخذ المثمن

BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r2.claim: Sale is named separately despite being included in trade because it is the more important of its two parts: profit is realized in a sale but only anticipated in a purchase, so if actual profit does not distract, potential profit will not.
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r2.anchor: وإفراده بالذكر مع اندراجه تحت التجارة لكونه أهم من قسمي التجارة فإن الربح يتحقق بالبيع ويتوقع بالشراء

BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r3.claim: Remembering God here means glorifying and praising Him.

BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r4.claim: Establishing prayer means performing it at its appointed times without delay.
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r4.anchor: أي إقامتها بمواقيتها من غير تأخير وقد سقطت التاء المعوضة عن العين الساقطة بالإعلال

BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r5.claim: The compensatory ta is dropped after the weak radical is lost through sound change, with the genitive construction compensating for it.
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r5.anchor: وقد سقطت التاء المعوضة عن العين الساقطة بالإعلال وعوض عنها الإضافة

BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r6.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says establishing prayer requires observing all legally prescribed pillars, conditions, sunnas, and etiquettes; neglecting any means one has not established it.
BURSEVI:v6p115#2/r6.anchor: ابن الشيخ : إقامة الصلاة اتمامها برعاية جميع ما اعتبره الشرع من الأركان

BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r1.claim: Zakat is the wealth required to be given to eligible recipients; it is mentioned with prayer although not performed in mosques because the two commonly go together.
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r1.anchor: أي : المال الذي فرض إخراجه للمستحقين وإيراده ههنا وإن لم يكن مما يفعل في البيوت

BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r2.claim: Fear is expecting something disliked on a probable or certain indication; hope is expectation of something desired, and safety opposes fear.
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r2.anchor: والخوف توقع مكروه عن أمارة مظنونة أو معلومة كما أن الرجاء والطمع توقع محبوب عن أمارة مظنونة أو معلومة

BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r3.claim: Yawman is the object of “they fear,” not an adverb of time, and refers to the Day of Resurrection.
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r3.anchor: مفعول ليخافون لا ظرف والمراد يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r4.claim: The hearts and eyes undergo terror, changing and shifting: hearts rise to throats, as 33:10 says, and eyes stare fixedly, as 14:42 says.
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r4.anchor: فتنقلب القلوب في الجوف وترتفع إلى الحنجرة ولا تنزل ولا تخرج

BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, hearts shift between hope of rescue and fear of destruction, while eyes scan where they will be taken or from which direction their records will arrive.
BURSEVI:v6p115#3/r5.anchor: أو تتقلب القلوب بين توقع النجاة وخوف الهلاك والأبصار من أي ناحية يؤخذ بهم ومن أي جهة يأتي كتابهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r9.claim: The following description of men glorifying God in the houses supports identifying them as mosques.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p185#2/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى: يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال رجال يقوي أنها المساجد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r7.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r7.claim: With the first reading, “rijāl” is subject of an implied verb indicated by “yusabbiḥu”; Sibawayh compares the construction to a poetic line meaning “a suppliant weeps for him.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r7.anchor: ف رجال على القراءة الأولى مرتفع بفعل مضمر يدل عليه يسبح تقديره يسبحه رجال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r8.claim: With the second reading, “rijāl” is the subject of the explicit verb “yusabbiḥu.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r8.anchor: ورجال على القراءة الثانية مرتفع ب يسبح الظاهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r13.claim: Their vigilance toward God and desire for His approval keep worldly affairs from distracting them from prayer and remembrance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r13.anchor: لمراقبتهم أمر الله تعالى وطلبهم لرضاه لا يشغلهم عن الصلاة وذكر الله شيء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r14.speaker: كثير من الصحابة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r14.claim: Many Companions said the verse concerns marketplace people who leave their work and hasten to prayer when they hear the call.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r14.anchor: وقال كثير من الصحابة نزلت هذه الآية في أهل الأسواق الذين إذا سمعوا النداء بالصلاة تركوا كل شغل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r15.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r15.claim: Salim ibn ʿAbd Allāh saw market-goers heading to prayer and said they were the people meant by the verse; the report is also related from Ibn Masʿūd.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r15.anchor: فرأى سالم بن عبد الله بن عمر أهل الأسواق وهم مقبلون إلى الصلاة فقال هؤلاء الذين أراد الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r16.claim: “Iqām” derives from “aqāma”: the original “aqwām” lost its wāw after its vowel shifted to qāf, where it met the following alif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r16.anchor: وإقام، مصدر من أقام يقيم أصله أقوام نقلت حركة الواو إلى القاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r17.speaker: الرماني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r17.claim: Al-Rummānī says “iqām” is itself a verbal noun, but “aqamtuhu iqāman” is not used; it appears in a construct phrase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r17.anchor: بعض النحويين هو مصدر بنفسه قد لا يضاف وقيل لا يجوز أقمته إقاما، وإنما يستعمل مضافا، ذكره الرماني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r18.claim: Some grammarians explain the tāʾ in “iqāma” as compensation for the deleted letter; it disappears in a construct phrase because the two words function as one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r18.anchor: ألحقت به هاء عوضا من المحذوف فجاء إقامة، فهم إذا أضافوه حذفوا العوض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets “zakāh” here as obedience to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r19.anchor: والزكاة هنا عند ابن عباس الطاعة لله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r20.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r20.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets it as the obligatory alms on wealth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r20.anchor: وقال الحسن هي الزكاة المفروضة في المال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r21.claim: The feared day is the Day of Resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r21.anchor: و «اليوم المخوف» الذي ذكره تعالى، هو يوم القيامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r22.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r22.claim: One group says people will see realities directly, turning doubters' hearts toward truth and changing their sight accordingly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r22.anchor: فقالت فرقة يرى الناس الحقائق عيانا فتتقلب قلوب الشاكين ومعتقدي الضلال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r23.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r23.claim: Another group says hearts and eyes will turn over the embers of Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186/r23.anchor: وقالت فرقة هو تقلبها على جمر جهنم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r1.speaker: الفقيه الإمام القاضي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the first group's account does not convey the terror intended by the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r1.anchor: فأما القول الأول فليس يقتضي هولا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r2.speaker: الفقيه الإمام القاضي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r2.claim: The second account occurs after the Day of Resurrection, not on that day as the verse says.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r2.anchor: وأما الثاني فليس التقلب في جمر جهنم في يوم القيامة وإنما هو بعده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r3.speaker: الفقيه الإمام القاضي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r3.claim: The verse describes hearts and eyes unsettled by the day's terror, shifting between hope of salvation, fear of ruin, and successive sights of horrors.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r3.anchor: أن ذلك اليوم لشدة هوله ومطلعه، القلوب والأبصار فيه مضطربة قلقة متقلبة من طمع في النجاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r4.speaker: الفقيه الإمام القاضي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Arabs use this description for the turmoil of wars and similar ordeals, citing poets who compare the heart to a bird's wings or a bouncing ball.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p186#2/r4.anchor: والعرب تستعمل هذا المعنى في الحروب ونحوها ومنه قول الشاعر: «بل كان قلبك في جناحي طائر»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r1.claim: Neither trade nor sales distract these men from worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى رجال لا تلهيهم أي لا تشغلهم تجارة ولا بيع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r2.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib calls the traveling merchants jallābūn and the settled sellers bāʾiʿūn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r2.anchor: قال ابن السائب التجار الجلابون والباعة المقيمون وقال الواقدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r3.speaker: الواقدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r3.claim: Al-Waqidi says trade here means buying.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r3.anchor: وقال الواقدي التجارة ها هنا بمعنى الشراء وفي المراد بذكر الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and ʿAtaʾ take remembrance of God to mean the obligatory prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r4.anchor: أحدها الصلاة المكتوبة قاله ابن عباس وعطاء وروى سالم عن ابن عمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r5.claim: Ibn Umar saw market traders close their shops and enter the mosque when prayer was called, and said this verse was revealed about them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r5.anchor: روى سالم عن ابن عمر أنه كان في السوق فأقيمت الصلاة فأغلقوا حوانيتهم ودخلوا المسجد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r6.claim: Qatada understands remembrance as fulfilling God's due rights.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r6.anchor: والثاني عن القيام بحق الله قاله قتادة والثالث عن ذكر الله باللسان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r7.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r7.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi understands it as remembering God with the tongue.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r7.anchor: قاله قتادة والثالث عن ذكر الله باللسان ذكره أبو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r8.claim: Establishing prayer means performing it at its proper time and completing it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r8.anchor: قوله تعالى وإقام الصلاة أي أداؤها لوقتها وإتمامها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r9.claim: If remembrance already means prayer, its repetition clarifies that they perform the prayer on time.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r9.anchor: أنه بين أنهم يقيمونها بأدائها في وقتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says believers in resurrection gain further insight on seeing what was promised, while others see what makes the Resurrection certain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r10.anchor: من كان قلبه مؤمنا بالبعث والنشور ازداد بصيرة برؤية ما وعد به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r11.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r11.claim: Ibn Jarir says hearts swing between hope of salvation and fear of ruin while eyes search where they will be taken and whether from the right or left.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r11.anchor: والثاني أن القلوب تتقلب بين الطمع في النجاة والخوف من الهلاك والأبصار تتقلب تنظر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r12.claim: A third view says hearts rise to throats and eyes turn blue after having been darkened with kohl, then blind after seeing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p47/r12.anchor: والثالث تتقلب القلوب فتبلغ إلى الحناجر وتتقلب الأبصار إلى الزرق بعد الكحل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r7.claim: In both Sahih collections, the Prophet says congregational prayer is twenty-five times better than prayer at home or in the market; each step toward the mosque raises rank and removes a sin, and angels pray for one who waits there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p64#2/r7.anchor: وقد ثبت في الصحيحين عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "صلاة الرجل في الجماعة تضعف على صلاته في بيته وفي سوقه، خمسا وعشرين ضعفا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r8.claim: Some readers vocalize yusabbaḥu passively with fath on bāʾ; they pause fully at al-asal and restart with rijāl, which explains the omitted agent. The cited verse uses the same implicit-agent construction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ من القرأة (1) " يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال" -بفتح الباء من "يسبح" على أنه مبني لما لم يسم فاعله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r9.speaker: الشاعر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r9.claim: The cited poetic line illustrates an understood agent: a question asks who bewails Yazid, then the following phrase supplies the answer. This supports the passive reading's restart with rijāl.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r9.anchor: ليبك يزيد، ضارع لخصومة … ومختبط مما تطيح الطوائح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r10.claim: Readers with kasra on the bāʾ read an active verb whose subject is rijāl; the pause is therefore suitable only after that subject completes the clause.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r10.anchor: وأما على قراءة من قرأ: {يسبح} -بكسر الباء -فجعله فعلا وفاعله: {رجال} فلا يحسن الوقف إلا على الفاعل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r11.claim: Rijāl signals their lofty aspirations, intentions, and resolve, which make them caretakers of God's mosques and places of worship, gratitude, oneness, and praise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p66/r11.anchor: فقوله: {رجال} فيه إشعار بهممهم السامية، ونياتهم وعزائمهم العالية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r2.claim: The prohibition against trade distracting from remembrance echoes the warning not to let wealth and children distract, and the command to leave trade for Friday prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r2.anchor: لا تشغلهم الدنيا وزخرفها وزينتها وملاذ بيعها وريحها، عن ذكر ربهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r3.claim: Worldly splendor, pleasures, and profitable sales do not distract these people from remembering their Creator and Provider; they know God’s lasting reward is better than perishable possessions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r3.anchor: لا تشغلهم الدنيا وزخرفها وزينتها وملاذ بيعها وريحها، عن ذكر ربهم الذي هو خالقهم ورازقهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r4.claim: They put God’s obedience, will, and love ahead of their own desires and affections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r4.anchor: يقدمون طاعته ومراده ومحبته على مرادهم ومحبتهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r5.claim: Hushaym reports through Sayyar that Ibn Masud saw market people leave their sales when prayer was called and identified them as those described in the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r5.anchor: حدثت عن ابن مسعود أنه رأى قوما من أهل السوق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r6.claim: Ibn Umar saw shopkeepers close their shops and enter the mosque when prayer was called, and said the verse was revealed about them; Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabari transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر، رضي الله عنهما، أنه كان في السوق (11) فأقيمت الصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
