IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r7.claim: Abu al-Darda says he earned three hundred dinars a day at his stall and attended mosque prayer daily; he did not call the trade unlawful but preferred the verse’s description.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p68/r7.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء، رضي الله عنه: إني قمت (5) على هذا الدرج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r1.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r1.claim: Amr ibn Dinar al-Awar reports that Salim saw Medina merchants cover their goods and attend prayer, then recited the verse and said it described them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r1.anchor: فمررنا بسوق المدينة وقد قاموا إلى الصلاة وخمروا متاعهم، فنظر سالم إلى أمتعتهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r2.speaker: سعيد بن أبي الحسن والضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r2.claim: Said ibn Abi al-Hasan and al-Dahhak explain that business does not distract them from performing prayer at its appointed time.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r2.anchor: وكذا قال سعيد بن أبي الحسن، والضحاك: لا تلهيهم التجارة والبيع أن يأتوا الصلاة في وقتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r3.speaker: مطر الوراق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r3.claim: Matar al-Warraq says they traded, but when the call came while a scale was in hand, they lowered it and went to prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r3.anchor: وقال مطر الوراق: كانوا يبيعون ويشترون، ولكن كان أحدهم إذا سمع النداء وميزانه في يده خفضه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, identifies remembrance of God here as the obligatory prayer; al-Rabi ibn Anas and Muqatil ibn Hayyan say the same.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r4.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس {لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} يقول: عن الصلاة المكتوبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r5.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the remembrance from which trade does not distract them as prayer in congregation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: عن الصلاة في جماعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r6.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r6.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says they attend prayer, establish it as God commanded, preserve its appointed times, and guard what God entrusted to them in it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69/r6.anchor: وعن مقاتل بن حيان: لا يلهيهم ذلك عن حضور الصلاة، وأن يقيموها كما أمرهم (6) الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69#2/r1.claim: The Day of Resurrection makes hearts and eyes turn from terror and immense horrors; Ibn Kathir links it with 40:18, 14:42, and the fearful day in 76:8–12.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p69#2/r1.anchor: أي: يوم القيامة الذي تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار، أي: من شدة الفزع وعظمة الأهوال

JISHUMI:v7p5205/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5205/r7.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v7p5205/r7.claim: The other readers read يسبح actively with kasra, making the men the ones who glorify God.
JISHUMI:v7p5205/r7.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بكسر الباء جعلوا التسبيح فعلا للرجال

JISHUMI:v7p5208/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar saw people close their shops and enter the mosque when prayer was called in the market, and said this verse was revealed about them.
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه كان في السوق فأقيمت الصلاة

JISHUMI:v7p5208/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r9.claim: The disbelievers’ example follows the believers’ example as its opposite, encouraging faith and warning against disbelief.
JISHUMI:v7p5208/r9.anchor: قلنا: اتصال النقيض بالنقيض، لما ضرب للمؤمنين مثلا وبين صفتهم عقبه بذكر الكفار

JISHUMI:v7p5216/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r1.claim: God commands establishing, maintaining, and frequenting mosques for worship and magnifies their caretakers' rank.
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r1.anchor: تدل الآية أنه تعالى تعبد باتخاذ المساجد وعمارتها وملازمتها للعبادة،

JISHUMI:v7p5216/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r2.claim: Worship is preferable to worldly activity, even when permitted.
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن الأولى الاشتغال بالعبادة دون أعمال الدنيا وإن كانت مباحة

JISHUMI:v7p5216/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r3.claim: Fear increases the excellence of worship.
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن العبادة تعظم مع الخوف

JISHUMI:v7p5216/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r4.claim: The feared day indicates the severity of the Day of Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v7p5216/r4.anchor: ويدل قوله: (يخافون يوما) على شدة يوم القيامة.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r14.claim: Tijāra is the trader’s craft of buying and selling for profit; sale is singled out because a profitable sale is the trader’s sure objective and distracts more than a purchase whose gain is only expected later.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r14.anchor: التجارة : صناعة التاجر ، وهو الذي يبيع ويشتري للربح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r15.claim: Trade may name buying as well as selling, using the general term for one type; another view limits it to caravan commerce and importing goods.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r15.anchor: وإما أن يسمى الشراء تجارة ، إطلاقا لاسم الجنس على النوع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r16.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r16.claim: Another explanation restricts tijāra to caravan merchants; itʿajara means to bring goods in.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r16.anchor: وقيل : التجارة لأهل الجلب ، اتجر فلان في كذا : إذا جلبه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r17.claim: The tāʾ in iqāma compensates for the root ʿayn dropped by defective morphology; the original is iqwām, and the construct form drops the compensating letter because the genitive relation takes its place, as in the cited poetic line.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p247/r17.anchor: التاء في إقامة ، عوض من العين الساقطة للإعلال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p248/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p248/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p248/r1.claim: Hearts and eyes may physically turn in terror and panic, as in 33:10; alternatively their conditions change, so sealed hearts understand and blind eyes see.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p248/r1.anchor: وتقلب القلوب والأبصار : إما أن تتقلب وتتغير في أنفسها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r14.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r14.claim: Al-Kalbi says the traders are traveling merchants and the sellers are residents.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r14.anchor: قال الكلبي : التجار هم الجلاب المسافرون , والباعة هم المقيمون .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r15.claim: “God's remembrance” may mean remembrance through His beautiful names.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r16.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r16.claim: Yahya ibn Salam interprets “God's remembrance” as the call to prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r16.anchor: الثاني : عن الأذان , قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r17.claim: One explanation is that hearts and eyes are turned over on the rocks of Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r17.anchor: أحدها : يعني تقلبها على حجر جهنم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r18.claim: Another explanation is the changing state of hearts and eyes as fire singes, roasts, and burns them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r18.anchor: الثاني : تقلب أحوالها بأن تلفحها النار ثم تنضجها وتحرقها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r19.claim: A third explanation is hearts beating anxiously and eyes scanning the surrounding terrors.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r19.anchor: الثالث : أن تقلب القلوب وجيبها , وتقلب الأبصار النظر بها إلى نواحي الأهوال .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r20.claim: A fourth explanation is hearts reaching the throats and eyes turning blue after being dark, or blind after sight.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r20.anchor: الرابع : أن تقلب القلوب بلوغها الحناجر , وتقلب الأبصار الزرق بعد الكحل ، والعمى بعد البصر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r21.claim: A fifth explanation is that after resurrection the unbeliever's heart changes from unbelief to faith and the eye sees guidance where it had seen error.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p106/r21.anchor: الخامس : أن الكافر بعد البعث ينقلب قلبه على الكفر إلى الإيمان وينقلب بصره عما كان يراه غيا فيراه رشدا .

MUQATIL:24:36-37/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r4.claim: The phrase has fronting: the morning and evening time expression precedes the description of the men.
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r4.anchor: رجال } فيها تقديم بالغدو والعشي، ثم نعتهم، فقال سبحانه:

MUQATIL:24:36-37/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r5.claim: Trade means buying, and remembrance of God means the obligatory prayers.
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r5.anchor: لا تلهيهم تجارة } يعني شراء { ولا بيع عن ذكر الله } يعني الصلوات المفروضة

MUQATIL:24:36-37/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r6.claim: Commerce does not distract them from establishing prayer or giving zakat.
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r6.anchor: لا تلهيهم التجارة عن إقام الصلاة، وإعطاء الزكاة، ثم أخبر عنهم،

MUQATIL:24:36-37/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r7.claim: On that day hearts leave their places in the chest and become lodged in people's throats at the larynx.
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r7.anchor: حين زالت من أماكنها من الصدور فنشبت في حلوقهم عند الحناجر

MUQATIL:24:36-37/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r8.claim: Their eyes turn and become blue.
MUQATIL:24:36-37/r8.anchor: والأبصار } [آية: 37] يعني تقلب أبصارهم فتكون زرقا.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r1.claim: Shami and Abu Bakr read the verb actively, making “men” its subject; the other reading is passive, with “men” raised by an understood verb.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ رجال ﴾ فاعل يسبح يسبح شامى وأبو بكر ويسند إلى أحد الظروف الثلاثة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r2.claim: On the passive reading, “men” is raised by what the wording implies: “men glorify God.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r2.anchor: ورجال مرفوع بمادل عليه يسبح أى يسبح له

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r3.claim: The phrase means that trade does not distract them.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r4.claim: Trade refers to travel and sale to activity at home; alternatively, trade means buying, while sale is singled out because its profit is more certain and therefore more distracting.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r4.anchor: ﴿ تجارة ﴾ فى السفر ﴿ ولا بيع ﴾ فى الحضر وقيل التجارة الشراء اطلاقا لاسم الجنس على النوع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r5.claim: Their remembrance of God is with both tongue and heart.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r6.claim: The tāʾ in iqāma replaces the dropped root letter; when the word is annexed, the genitive construction replaces the tāʾ.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r6.anchor: التاء فى إقامة عوض من العين الساقطة للأعلال الأصل أقوام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r7.claim: The phrase means that neither trade nor sale distracts them from giving zakat.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r7.anchor: ﴿ وإيتاء الزكاة ﴾ أى وعن إيتاء الزكاة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r8.claim: One possibility is that they do no buying or selling, like the devoted solitary; another is that they trade while remembering God and promptly rise for prayer, like the sociable devoted.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r8.anchor: والمعنى لا تجارة لهم حتى تلهيهم كأولياء العزلة أو يبيعون ويشترون ويذكرون الله مع ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r9.claim: “Fearing a day” may be circumstantial from the pronoun in “distracts them” or another adjective describing the men.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r9.anchor: ويخافون حال من الضمير في تلهيهم أو صفة أخرى لرجال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r10.claim: Hearts may turn by rising to the throats and eyes by staring and turning blue; alternatively, hearts turn from disbelief to faith and eyes from denial to direct vision, as in the verse about the lifted veil.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p148#3/r10.anchor: ﴿ تتقلب فيه القلوب ﴾ ببلوغها إلى الجناجر ﴿ والأبصار ﴾ بالشخوص والزرقة أو تتقلب القلوب إلى الإيمان بعد الكفران

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r4.speaker: كثير من الصحابة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r4.claim: Many Companions say the verse was revealed about market people who leave their work and hasten to prayer when they hear the call; Salim ibn Abdullah saw Ibn Umar's market witnesses as its intended men, and it is also reported from Ibn Masud.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r4.anchor: وقال كثير من الصحابة: نزلت هذه الآية في أهل الأسواق الذين إذا سمعوا النداء بالصلاة تركوا كل شغل وبادروا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r6.claim: On the passive reading, رجال may be subject of an implied verb, allowing a pause at الآصال, as in Sibawayh's poetic analogy; alternatively رجال is initial subject, في بيوت its predicate, and the verb a circumstantial clause, without a pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-37#2/r6.anchor: أحدهما أن يرتفع «رجال» بفعل مضمر دل عليه الظاهر بمعنى يسبحه رجال فيوقف على هذا على «الآصال» وقد ذكر سيبويه

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r1.speaker: أبو أمامة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r1.claim: The Prophet says that leaving home purified for an obligatory prayer earns the reward of a pilgrim in ihram; setting out solely for Duha earns that of an Umrah pilgrim, and prayer after prayer without idle speech is recorded in Illiyyin.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r1.anchor: من خرج من بيته متطهرا إلى صلاة مكتوبة فأجره كأجر الحاج المحرم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r2.speaker: بريدة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r2.claim: The Prophet gives glad tidings of complete light on Judgment Day to those who walk to mosques in darkness.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r2.anchor: بشر المشائين في الظلم إلى المساجد بالنور التام يوم القيامة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r3.claim: The Prophet promises a welcome in Paradise each time someone visits a mosque morning or evening; al-Tha'labi also cites an extra comparison to a host honoring a loved visitor, which Qurtubi labels unauthentic.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r3.anchor: من غدا إلى المسجد أو راح أعد الله له نزلا في الجنة كلما غدا أو راح

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r4.claim: The Prophet says each step of one who purifies at home and walks to a mosque for an obligation erases a sin or raises a degree.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r4.anchor: من تطهر في بيته ثم مشى إلى بيت من بيوت الله ليقضي فريضة من فرائض الله كانت خطوتاه

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r5.claim: The Prophet says congregational prayer exceeds prayer at home or in the market by more than twenty degrees; each step earns reward, and angels pray for the worshipper who remains in the prayer place without harm or breaking wind.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r5.anchor: صلاة الرجل في جماعة تزيد على صلاته في بيته وصلاته في سوقه بضعا وعشرين درجة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r6.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says attending a funeral earns one or two qirats, but sitting in the mosque is dearer because the angels pray for mercy and forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#6/r6.anchor: قال حكيم بن زريق: قيل لسعيد بن المسيب أحضور الجنازة أحب إليك أم الجلوس في المسجد؟ فقال: من صلى على جنازة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r9.claim: Qurtubi infers from mentioning men that women have no share in mosque attendance, since Friday and congregational prayers are not incumbent on them, and says prayer at home is better for them.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r9.anchor: السادسة عشرة: لما قال تعالى: «رجال» وخصهم بالذكر دل على أن النساء لا حظ لهن في المساجد إذ لا جمعة عليهن ولا جماعة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r10.speaker: عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r10.claim: The Prophet says a woman's prayer at home is better than in her room, and prayer in her private chamber is better still.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:36-38#8/r10.anchor: روى أبو داود عن عبد الله رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r1.claim: Qurtubi says trade is singled out because it is the greatest distraction; since sale follows it, he reports al-Waqidi's explanation that trade here means buying.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r1.anchor: قيل له: أراد بالتجارة الشراء لقوله: «ولا بيع».

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r2.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi distinguishes the traveling importers as traders and the resident merchants as sellers.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: التجار هم الجلاب المسافرون، والباعة هم المقيمون.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r3.speaker: عطاء وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r3.claim: Ata and Ibn Abbas interpret remembrance of God as attending the obligatory prayer; Yahya ibn Sallam instead says it means the call to prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r3.anchor: فقال عطاء: يعني حضور الصلاة وقاله ابن عباس، وقال: المكتوبة.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes remembrance of God as invoking His beautiful names, declaring His oneness, and glorifying Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r4.anchor: وقيل: عن ذكره بأسمائه الحسنى أي يوحدونه ويمجدونه.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r5.claim: Ibn Umar identifies market people as the occasion of revelation; Salim recounts that Ibn Umar saw them close their shops and rise for congregational prayer, saying they were the men of the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r5.anchor: والآية نزلت في أهل الأسواق قاله ابن عمر. قال سالم: جاز عبد الله بن عمر بالسوق وقد أغلقوا حوانيتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r6.claim: Abu Huraira reports the Prophet identifying the men as those who travel the earth seeking God's bounty.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r6.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: هم الذين يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r7.claim: An account describes two men who stopped their work when they heard the prayer call: a seller left his scales and a swordsmith put down or cast away his hammer; the verse praises them and their imitators.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن رجلين كانا في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، أحدهما بياعا فإذا سمع النداء بالصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r8.claim: Qurtubi says adding establishment of prayer shows remembrance here means something other than prayer, avoiding redundancy; إقامة derives from إقوام with vowel shift, deletion of an alif, and compensatory tāʾ, which drops in an إضافة construction; al-Farra's cited verse witnesses deletion of hā from عدة in إضافة.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37/r8.anchor: يقال: أقام الصلاة إقامة، والأصل إقواما فقلبت حركة الواو على القاف

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the zakat in the verse as the obligatory alms.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets zakat here as obedience to God and sincerity, since not every believer has wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الزكاة هنا طاعة الله تعالى والإخلاص إذ ليس لكل مؤمن مال.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r3.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r3.claim: Anas reports a Prophetic scene in which the world's mosques appear at the Resurrection as radiant mounts led by their callers and imams and carried by their worshippers, who pass the plain like lightning.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r3.anchor: وروي من حديث أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r4.claim: Ali warns that Islam will remain only in name and Quran in script, while mosques are built but empty of God's remembrance; the scholars will spread turmoil because they do not practice what they teach.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r4.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال: يأتي على الناس زمان لا يبقى من الإسلام إلا اسمه، ولا من القرآن إلا رسمه، يعمرون مساجدهم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r5.claim: The day feared is the Day of Resurrection, whose terror and fear of destruction make hearts and eyes turn about.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r5.anchor: يخافون يوما } يعني يوم القيامة. { تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار } يعني من هوله وحذر الهلاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r6.claim: Qurtubi says the hearts and eyes are those of disbelievers: hearts are pulled from their places to throats, neither returning nor emerging, while eyes turn blue or become blind after sight.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r6.anchor: والمراد قلوب الكفار وأبصارهم. فتقلب القلوب انتزاعها من أماكنها إلى الحناجر، فلا هي ترجع إلى أماكنها

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r7.claim: Another view says hearts waver between hope of salvation and fear of ruin, while eyes look to see from which direction they will receive their books and be taken.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: تتقلب القلوب بين الطمع في النجاة والخوف من الهلاك، والأبصار تنظر من أي ناحية يعطون كتبهم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r8.claim: A further view says doubters' hearts change from doubt and their eyes perceive certainty, as in Q 50:22, when the veil is removed; what seemed error in life may appear guidance, but this will not benefit them then.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن قلوب الشاكين تتحول عما كانت عليه من الشك، وكذلك أبصارهم لرؤيتهم اليقين وذلك مثل قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r9.claim: One more interpretation says hearts are turned over on the embers of Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:37#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: تقلب على جمر جهنم كقوله تعالى:

QASHANI:24:36-38/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:24:36-38/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:24:36-38/r5.claim: The men are singular spiritual exemplars: advanced, detached and individuated, established in the Real.
QASHANI:24:36-38/r5.anchor: أي: رجال أفراد سابقون مجردون مفردون قائمون بالحق

QASHANI:24:36-38/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:24:36-38/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:24:36-38/r6.claim: Their commerce does not trade the afterlife for this world through asceticism, and their sale is of selves and wealth for promised paradise in spiritual struggle; neither distracts from remembrance of the Essence.
QASHANI:24:36-38/r6.anchor: باستبدال متاع العقبى بالدنيا في زهدهم، ولا بيع أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة في جهادهم

QASHANI:24:36-38/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:24:36-38/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:24:36-38/r7.claim: Prayer is witnessing in annihilation, while zakat is guidance and spiritual completion during subsistence.
QASHANI:24:36-38/r7.anchor: صلاة الشهود في الفناء { وإيتاء } زكاة الإرشاد والتكميل حال البقاء

QASHANI:24:36-38/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:24:36-38/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:24:36-38/r8.claim: Hearts turn toward secrets and eyes toward inner perceptions; their realities are annihilated and made existent through the Real, as in the report that God becomes the servant's hearing and sight.
QASHANI:24:36-38/r8.anchor: إلى الأسرار { والأبصار } إلى البصائر، بل تتقلب حقائقها بأن تفنى وتوجد بالحق، كما قال: " كنت سمعه وبصره "

RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r12.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj see no ellipsis, but fronting and delay: men of the described kind glorify God in the houses.
RAZI-FULL:v24p3/r12.anchor: قول الفراء والزجاج إنه لا حذف في الآية بل فيه تقديم وتأخير

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r2.claim: With the passive reading the statement continues through the time phrases; al-Zajjāj explains rijāl as the answer to “who glorifies in them?”
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r2.anchor: مرفوع لأنه لما قال { يسبح له فيها }

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r13.claim: One view says these men are not merchants or sellers at all.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r13.anchor: فقال بعضهم نفى كونهم تجارا وباعة أصلا

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r14.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r14.claim: The majority say they trade, but no commercial benefit distracts them from remembrance, prayer, or zakat.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r14.anchor: وقال بعضهم بل أثبتهم تجارا وباعة وبين أنهم مع ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r15.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they traded, but when God’s obligations came, nothing distracted them; they prayed and paid zakat.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r15.anchor: قال الحسن أما والله إن كانوا ليتجرون

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r16.speaker: سالم
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r16.claim: Sālim saw market people leave their sales and go to prayer, identifying them as those described in the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r16.anchor: وعن سالم نظر إلى قوم من أهل السوق

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r17.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r17.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is reported to have made the same observation about people leaving business for prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r17.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود مثله ، واعلم أن هذا القول أولى

RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r18.claim: Rāzī prefers the view that they are traders: one says trade does not distract someone from a duty only when that person actually trades.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5/r18.anchor: أنه لا يقال إن فلانا لا تلهيه التجارة عن كيت وكيت

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r1.claim: Trade includes buying and selling, but sale is named because its certain, immediate profit distracts more than the uncertain future gain of purchase.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r1.anchor: أن التجارة جنس يدخل تحت أنواع الشراء والبيع إلا أنه / سبحانه خص البيع بالذكر

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r2.claim: Sale exchanges goods for cash, while purchase reverses that exchange; desire for acquiring cash is stronger.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r2.anchor: أن البيع يقتضي تبديل العرض بالنقد ، والشراء بالعكس

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says trade is importing goods from another place, while sale is what a person sells with his own hands.

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r4.claim: Men are specified because al-Rāzī says women are not among those engaged in commerce or congregational gatherings.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r4.anchor: لأن النساء لسن من أهل التجارات أو الجماعات

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r5.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r5.claim: One view takes remembrance of God to mean praising Him and making supplications.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r5.anchor: فقال قوم : المراد الثناء على الله تعالى والدعوات

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r6.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r6.claim: Another view takes remembrance of God to mean the prayers themselves.

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains establishing prayer as performing it at its appointed times.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما المراد بإقام الصلاة إقامتها لمواقيتها

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī allows “righteousness is not…” to explain remembrance: they remember God before prayer and during it.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r8.anchor: يجوز أن يكون قوله : { ليس البر }

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r9.claim: Establishing prayer means fulfilling its due rights according to its conditions, as al-Rāzī explained under al-Baqara 2:3.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r9.anchor: إقام الصلاة هو القيام بحقها على شروطها

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives iqāma from aqāma: the wāw becomes alif, one adjacent alif is deleted, and tāʾ compensates for the deletion.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r10.anchor: ما قاله الزجاج ، يقال أقمت الصلاة إقامة

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r11.claim: The genitive construction compensates for the deleted tāʾ; al-Rāzī says grammarians unanimously accept the analysis.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r11.anchor: وقامت الإضافة ههنا في التعويض مقام الهاء المحذوفة ، قال وهذا إجماع من النحويين

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r12.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r12.claim: One view restricts prayer here to obligatory prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r12.anchor: اختلفوا في الصلاة فمنهم من قال هي الفرائض

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r13.claim: Another view includes voluntary prayer, as in the cited report from Ibn ʿAbbās about the ḍuḥā prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r13.anchor: على ما حكيناه في صلاة الضحى عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r14.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers obligatory prayer because it is more precise as a definition and matches the established legal term.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r14.anchor: والأول أقرب لأنه إلى التعريف أقرب وكذلك القول في الزكاة أن المراد المفروض

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r15.claim: Zakat means the obligatory due, the established legal meaning of the term; its connection to giving points to a property payment.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r15.anchor: المراد المفروض لأنه المعروف في الشرع المسمى بذلك

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives zakat the broader sense of obeying God and sincerity, also applying that sense in the cited verses.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r16.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما المراد من الزكاة طاعة الله تعالى والإخلاص

RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r17.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the broad sense: zakat is connected to giving and therefore denotes what is paid from property.
RAZI-FULL:v24p5#2/r17.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لما تقدم ولأنه تعالى علق الزكاة بالإيتاء

RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r1.claim: Though devoted to remembrance and worship, these men fear Judgment Day because they know they have not worshipped God as He deserves.
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r1.anchor: هؤلاء الرجال وإن تعبدوا بذكر الله والطاعات فإنهم مع ذلك موصوفون بالوجل والخوف

RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r2.speaker: القول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r2.claim: The first explanation is that hearts convulse with terror and eyes stare in horror.
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r2.anchor: فالقول الأول أن القلوب تضطرب من الهول والفزع وتشخص الأبصار

RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r3.speaker: القول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r3.claim: Hearts and eyes change: the previously uncomprehending heart understands and the formerly blind eye sees, moving from doubt to certainty and then direct witnessing.
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r3.anchor: الثاني : أنها تتغير أحوالها فتفقه القلوب بعد أن كانت مطبوعا عليها لا تفقه

RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r4.speaker: القول الثالث
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r4.claim: Hearts swing between hope of rescue and fear of ruin, while eyes turn anxiously toward where people will be led and where their books will come from.
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r4.anchor: الثالث : أن القلوب تتقلب في ذلك اليوم طمعا في النجابة وحذرا من الهلاك

RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r5.claim: The Muʿtazilites reject the third explanation: the saved have no fear and the punished do not hope for pardon; al-Rāzī says he has already refuted their position.
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r5.anchor: والمعتزلة لا يرضون بهذا التأويل ، فإنهم قالوا إن أهل الثواب لا خوف عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r6.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the disbeliever is raised with keen sight, his eyes turn blue and then go blind, and fear drives his heart up to his throat.
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r6.anchor: قال الضحاك : يحشر الكافر وبصره حديد وتزرق عيناه ثم يعمى

RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r7.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r7.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says punishment changes the hearts’ and eyes’ appearance, like flesh being roasted or burned; he also allows that they turn over Hellfire’s embers.
RAZI-FULL:v24p6/r7.anchor: قال الجبائي المراد بتقلب القلوب والأبصار تغير هيئاتهما بسبب ما ينالها من العذاب

STUDYQURAN:24:37/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r1.claim: The wording parallels 63:9's warning not to let property or children divert from God's remembrance and 62:9's command to leave trade for Friday prayer.
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r1.anchor: The language here is similar to that in 63:9: Let neither your property nor your children divert you from the remembrance of God; and 62:9

STUDYQURAN:24:37/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r2.claim: The turning about of eyes and hearts refers to the terror and awe of Judgment Day.
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r2.anchor: The phrase when eyes and hearts will be turned about refers to the terror and awe experienced on the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:24:37/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r3.claim: The imagery recalls 14:42–43, where eyes stare transfixed and hearts are vacant on the Day of Judgment.
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r3.anchor: related imagery is used to describe eyes and hearts in 14:42–43

STUDYQURAN:24:37/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r4.speaker: Sufis
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r4.claim: Continuing the symbolism, houses can represent the hearts of people who fear being turned away from God's remembrance.
STUDYQURAN:24:37/r4.anchor: the houses can be said to symbolize the hearts of those who are afraid of their eyes and hearts being turned away from the remembrance of God

QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r11.claim: The verse does not forbid trade or sale; combining them with remembrance is unobjectionable, though the greatest are absorbed in the affairs that pass over them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r11.anchor: لم يقل : لا يتجرون ولا يشترون ولا يبيعون ، بل قال : لا تلهيهم تجارة

QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r12.claim: They are also described as those who give God’s rights precedence over the self’s interests.
QUSHAYRI:v2p369/r12.anchor: ويقال هم الذين يؤثرون حقوق الحق على حظوظ النفس

QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r1.claim: When the call to prayer sounds, these people leave trade and sale and rise to fulfill their duty.
QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r1.anchor: إذا سمعوا صوت المؤذن : حي على الصلاة تركوا ما هم فيه من التجارة والبيع ، وقاموا الأداء حقه

QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r2.claim: The elect are not distracted even by the promised trade that saves from punishment; they remember God without seeking compensation or an instrumental cause.
QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r2.anchor: هم الخواص والأكابر الذين لا يشغلهم قوله : { هل أدلكم على تجارة تنجيكم

QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r3.claim: For some the fearful Day is still to come; for others it is immediate in their present moment, since true fear anticipates punishment with every breath.
QUSHAYRI:v2p370/r3.anchor: أقوام ذلك اليوم مؤجل لهم ، وآخرون : ذلك لهم معجل وهو بحسب ما هم فيه من الوقت

TAB-FULL:v17p317/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers mosques because the following description of men praying there shows these are houses built for prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p317/r4.anchor: لدلالة قوله: {يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} [النور: 37] على أنها بيوت بنيت للصلاة

TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the active reading with رجال as the verb's subject because the report about the houses is already complete without this clause.
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r3.anchor: والقراءة التي هي أولاهما بالصواب: قراءة من كسر الباء، وجعله خبرا ل (الرجال) وفعلا لهم

TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says God authorized these houses to be built so people could pray in them morning and evening.
TAB-FULL:v17p319#2/r7.anchor: عن الحسن: { يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال رجال} [النور: 37] «أذن الله أن تبنى، فيصلى فيها بالغدو والآصال»

TAB-FULL:v17p322/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r1.claim: Men who pray in these mosques are not distracted by trade or sale from remembering God there and establishing prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم: معنى ذلك {لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع} [النور: 37] عن صلاتهم المفروضة عليهم

TAB-FULL:v17p322/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r2.speaker: رجل نسي اسمه
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r2.claim: An unnamed man describes them as people whose commercial work does not distract them from God's remembrance.
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r2.anchor: عن رجل، نسي اسمه في هذه الآية:

TAB-FULL:v17p322/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r3.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r3.claim: Salim ibn Abd Allah saw market sellers leave their sales for prayer and identified them as those described in the verse.
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r3.anchor: عن سالم بن عبد الله: أنه نظر إلى قوم من السوق قاموا وتركوا بياعاتهم إلى الصلاة، فقال: " هؤلاء الذين ذكر الله في كتابه:

TAB-FULL:v17p322/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r4.claim: Ibn Masud saw market people leave their sales when prayer was called and identified them with the verse.
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r4.anchor: حدثت عن ابن مسعود: أنه رأى قوما من أهل السوق حيث نودي بالصلاة تركوا بياعاتهم , ونهضوا إلى الصلاة، فقال عبد الله: " هؤلاء من الذين ذكر الله في كتابه

TAB-FULL:v17p322/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r5.claim: Some interpret remembrance here specifically as the obligatory prayers that trade and sale do not distract them from.
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: معنى ذلك {لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع} [النور: 37] عن صلاتهم المفروضة عليهم

TAB-FULL:v17p322/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses remembrance here as the prescribed prayer.
TAB-FULL:v17p322/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: ثم قال: {رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله} [النور: 37] يقول: «عن الصلاة المكتوبة»

TAB-FULL:v17p323/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p323/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p323/r1.claim: Trade does not prevent them from performing prayer properly and observing its appointed times.

TAB-FULL:v17p323/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p323/r2.speaker: رجل نسي عوف اسمه
TAB-FULL:v17p323/r2.claim: An unnamed man says they rise for prayer when its appointed times arrive.
TAB-FULL:v17p323/r2.anchor: عن رجل، نسي عوف اسمه في: {وإقام الصلاة} [الأنبياء: 73] قال: «يقومون للصلاة عند مواقيت الصلاة»

TAB-FULL:v17p323/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p323/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p323/r3.claim: The expected verbal noun is iqwām; wāw drops when it meets sukun, a compensatory tāʾ is added, then removed in annexation, as in the poet's omission of tāʾ in عدّة الأمر.
TAB-FULL:v17p323/r3.anchor: قيل: ولكني أجيز: أعجبني إقام الصلاة.

TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r1.claim: On that terrifying day, hearts swing between hope for salvation and fear of destruction.
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r1.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم، في قول الله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] . إلى قوله: {تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار} [النور: 37] «يوم القيامة»

TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r2.claim: People's eyes turn toward right or left as they are led, while they wonder from which side they will receive their records.
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r2.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم، في قول الله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] . إلى قوله: {تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار} [النور: 37] «يوم القيامة»

TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies the day described from the houses passage through the turning hearts and eyes as the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v17p325#2/r3.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم، في قول الله: {في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع} [النور: 36] . إلى قوله: {تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار} [النور: 37] «يوم القيامة»

SULAMI:v2p53/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p53/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p53/r1.claim: These men are repositories of entrusted things and places where secrets are kept.
SULAMI:v2p53/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : خزائن الودائع ، ومواضع الأسرار

SULAMI:v2p53/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p53/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p53/r2.claim: Their hearts are attached to divine foreordinings and outcomes; grief over their beginning and their final return keeps them from worldly occupation and enjoyment.
SULAMI:v2p53/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : رجال قلوبهم متعلقة بالسوابق والخواتيم

SULAMI:v2p53/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p53/r3.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v2p53/r3.claim: The Creator has removed concern with created things from them, so causes do not distract them from the Causer.
SULAMI:v2p53/r3.anchor: سمعت النصرآباذي يقول في هذه الآية : رجال اسقط عنهم المكون ذكر المكنونات

SULAMI:v2p53/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p53/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p53/r4.claim: True men are guarded by God from turning their innermost selves toward anything else; neither worldly commerce and delights nor afterlife reward distract them from the gardens of intimacy and remembrance.
SULAMI:v2p53/r4.anchor: وقال جعفر : هم الرجال من بين الرجال عن الحقيقة لأن الله حفظ سرائرهم

SULAMI:v2p53/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p53/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p53/r5.claim: God reserves the title of men among worshippers for those who serve Him in direct witnessing and give no preference to created things.
SULAMI:v2p53/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أسقط الله اسم الرجولية عن العاملين إلا من عامل الله

SULAMI:v2p53/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p53/r6.speaker: الواسطى
SULAMI:v2p53/r6.claim: Al-Wasiti distinguishes remembrance of divine overpowering, which brings fear and grief; remembrance of the divine hand, grace, and precedence; and remembrance of witnessing, which is the remembrance of men.
SULAMI:v2p53/r6.anchor: قال الواسطى رحمه الله : الأذكار ثلاثة :

SULAMI:v2p53#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r1.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r1.claim: Souls undergo transfer, while hearts undergo turning.
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r1.anchor: سمعت النصرآباذي يقول : النفوس في التنقيل ، والقلوب في التقليب

SULAMI:v2p53#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r2.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r2.claim: God made hearts and eyes changeable, but covers and locks them; He tears veils with lights, lifts them through remembrance, and opens locks through nearness.
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r2.anchor: قال الحسين : خلق الله القلوب ، والأبصار على التقلب

SULAMI:v2p53#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r3.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r3.claim: Knowing God turns hearts and eyes should make one attend to His acts within oneself and guard against opposition and heedlessness.
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسين : إذا علمت أنه مقلب القلوب والأبصار فليكن شغلك في النظر إلى أفعاله

SULAMI:v2p53#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r4.speaker: الواسطى
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r4.claim: For ordinary people, hearts turn on that Day in fear of the rejection of their deeds; the source links this to 39:47, when what they did not expect appears to them.
SULAMI:v2p53#2/r4.anchor: قال الواسطى رحمه الله : يخافون يوما تتقلب فيه القلوب للعامة تتقلب قلوبهم حذرا لما يرد

TUSTARI:24:37/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:24:37/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:24:37/r1.claim: The day is the Resurrection, when hearts and eyes pass from state to state and find no lasting condition; believers fear it.
TUSTARI:24:37/r1.anchor: يعني يوم البعث تتقلب فيه القلوب والأبصار حالا بعد حال لا يدومون على حال

TUSTARI:24:37/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:24:37/r2.speaker: الحسن
TUSTARI:24:37/r2.claim: When told that a man would emerge from Hell after a thousand years, al-Hasan wished that he himself might be that man.
TUSTARI:24:37/r2.anchor: وقد حكي عن الحسن أنه قال: ذكر عنده أن رجلا يخرج من النار

TUSTARI:24:37/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:24:37/r3.speaker: عون بن عبد الله
TUSTARI:24:37/r3.claim: ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh relates Luqman's counsel to hope in God without feeling secure from His plan and fear Him without despairing of mercy; the believer has one heart for hope and one for fear.
TUSTARI:24:37/r3.anchor: حكي عن عون بن عبدالله أنه قال: أوصى لقمان ابنه

TABATABAI:24:35-37/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-37/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-37/r9.claim: In context, ‘whomever He wills’ refers to the men described next as fully faithful, including those not distracted from God’s remembrance by trade or sale.
TABATABAI:24:35-37/r9.anchor: فمن المعلوم من السياق أن المراد بقوله { من يشاء } القوم الذين ذكرهم

TABATABAI:24:35-37/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:35-37/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:35-37/r10.claim: This does not mean God arbitrarily selects some individuals and then requires a separate appeal to their receptivity; the context identifies the guided with people of complete faith.
TABATABAI:24:35-37/r10.anchor: وليس المعنى أن الله يهدي بعض الأفراد إلى نوره دون بعض بمشيئة ذلك حتى يحتاج في تتميمه إلى القول بأنه إنما يشاء الهداية

TABRISI:24:36-37/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r13.claim: The men are not occupied or diverted by trade or sale from remembering God and establishing prayer.

TABRISI:24:36-37/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r14.claim: In iqām al-ṣalāh, the feminine ending is omitted because it replaces the wāw in aqwām; annexation supplies the ending's role.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r14.anchor: أي إقامة الصلاة حذف الهاء لأنها عوض عن الواو

TABRISI:24:36-37/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r15.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
TABRISI:24:36-37/r15.claim: They are people who leave trade and go to prayer when its time arrives, earning more than those who continue trading.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r15.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر ع وأبي عبد الله ع أنهم قوم إذا حضرت الصلاة تركوا التجارة وانطلقوا إلى الصلاة

TABRISI:24:36-37/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:24:36-37/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas explains giving alms as sincere obedience to God.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r16.anchor: أي إخلاص الطاعة لله تعالى عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:24:36-37/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r17.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:24:36-37/r17.claim: Al-Hasan takes the phrase to mean the obligatory alms-tax.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r17.anchor: وقيل: يريد الزكاة المفروضة عن الحسن

TABRISI:24:36-37/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r18.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:24:36-37/r18.claim: The day is the Resurrection, when hearts and eyes pass through changing states as the Fire scorches, roasts, and burns them.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r18.anchor: أراد يوم القيامة تتقلب فيه أحوال القلوب والأبصار وتنتقل من حال إلى حال فتلفحها النار

TABRISI:24:36-37/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r19.claim: Another view says hearts swing between hope of rescue and fear of ruin, while eyes look right and left to learn where books and people will be taken.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r19.anchor: وقيل: تتقلب فيه القلوب بين الطمع في النجاة والخوف من الهلاك

TABRISI:24:36-37/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r20.claim: A further view says hearts rise to the throats and sight becomes blindness after seeing.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r20.anchor: وقيل: تتقلب القلوب ببلوغها الحناجر والأبصار بالعمى بعد البصر

TABRISI:24:36-37/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:36-37/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:36-37/r21.claim: Another reading takes the change as hearts moving from doubt to faith and eyes seeing guidance where they formerly saw error; the insightful gain further insight.
TABRISI:24:36-37/r21.anchor: وقيل: معناه تنتقل القلوب عن الشك إلى اليقين والإيمان

FARRA:v2p253/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p253/r3.speaker: التفسير
FARRA:v2p253/r3.claim: The tafsīr distinguishes caravan commerce from what a man sells with his own hands.

FARRA:v2p253/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p253/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p253/r4.claim: A worldly doubter will see the truth in the next life; a person who did not doubt gains heart-sight there, explaining the change.
FARRA:v2p253/r4.anchor: من كان في دنياه شاكا أبصر ذلك في أمر آخرته، ومن كان لا يشك ازداد قلبه بصرا

FARRA:v2p253/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p253/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p253/r7.claim: Deficient triliteral afʿala verbal nouns usually retain final tāʾ: إقامة، إجارة، إجابة; it compensates for the dropped middle radical.
FARRA:v2p253/r7.anchor: المصدر من ذوات الثلاثة إذا قلت: أفعلت

FARRA:v2p253/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p253/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p253/r8.claim: The tāʾ may drop from إقام الصلاة in a construct because the governed noun and genitive are one unit; compensatory tāʾ also appears in عدة and related forms.
FARRA:v2p253/r8.anchor: وإنما استجيز سقوط الهاء من قوله (وإقام الصلاة) لإضافتهم إياه، وقالوا: الخافض وما خفض بمنزلة الحرف الواحد.

THALABI:v7p107/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p107/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p107/r12.claim: On the passive reading, men is supplied as the delayed agent; the pause falls at evenings. Other readers use the active, making glorification the men's action.
THALABI:v7p107/r12.anchor: والوقف على هذه القراءة عند قوله والآصال. وقرأ الآخرون بكسر الباء جعلوا التسبيح فعلا للرجال

THALABI:v7p108/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p108/r1.speaker: سهل بن سعد الساعدي
THALABI:v7p108/r1.claim: Sahl ibn Sa'd reports that one who goes to the mosque to learn or teach good is like a returning victorious fighter, while one going for another purpose sees worshippers without belonging to them.
THALABI:v7p108/r1.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من غدا الى المسجد وراح ليتعلم خيرا

THALABI:v7p108/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p108/r2.speaker: قائل
THALABI:v7p108/r2.claim: One explanation singles out men because women are not obligated to attend Friday or congregational prayers in mosques.
THALABI:v7p108/r2.anchor: قيل: وجه تخصيص الرجال بالذكر في هذه البيوت أنه ليس على النساء جمعة ولا جماعة

THALABI:v7p108/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p108/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v7p108/r3.claim: The People of Meaning say commerce is singled out because it is the greatest distraction from prayers and other acts of devotion.
THALABI:v7p108/r3.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: إنما خص التجارات لأنها أعظم ما يشتغل بها الإنسان عن الصلوات

THALABI:v7p108/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p108/r4.speaker: الواقدي
THALABI:v7p108/r4.claim: In answer to why sale is named alongside trade, al-Waqidi says trade here means purchase, as in the verse about seeing trade.
THALABI:v7p108/r4.anchor: فالجواب عنه ما قال الواقدي أنه أراد بالتجارة الشراء نظيره قوله سبحانه وإذا رأوا تجارة

THALABI:v7p108/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p108/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p108/r5.claim: Iqamat al-salat drops its final h in annexation: the suffix originally compensates for deleted waw in the form aqwama, whose waw was dropped after a heavy vowel and transferred to qaf; annexation then replaces the h, as with ida and zina.
THALABI:v7p108/r5.anchor: لأن أصل الكلمة أقومت إقواما فاستثقلوا الضمة على الواو فسكنوها فاجتمع حرفان ساكنان

THALABI:v7p108/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p108/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p108/r6.claim: A line by al-A'sha supports dropping the h from idda when the noun is annexed: the phrase means the appointed term of what they promised.
THALABI:v7p108/r6.anchor: كقول الشاعر: إن الخليط أجدوا البين وانجردوا

THALABI:v7p108/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p108/r7.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v7p108/r7.claim: Al-Hasan takes the zakat here to mean the obligatory alms.

THALABI:v7p108/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p108/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p108/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets zakat as sincere obedience to God.
THALABI:v7p108/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الزكاة إخلاص الطاعة لله سبحانه وتعالى

THALABI:v7p108/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p108/r9.speaker: ابن حيان
THALABI:v7p108/r9.claim: Ibn Hayyan identifies the men as the People of the Suffa.
THALABI:v7p108/r9.anchor: قال ابن حيان: هم أهل الصفة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p305#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p305#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p305#2/r1.claim: On that Day hearts turn from their worldly states of doubt and disbelief, and eyes are opened as their coverings are removed.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p305#2/r1.anchor: تتقلب عما كانت عليه في الدنيا: من الشك والكفر؛ وتتفتح فيه الأبصار من الأغطية.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r1.claim: رجال is nominative as the subject of يسبح.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r3.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r3.claim: The verse ليبك يزيد ضارع illustrates a verb implying an agent and identifying it afterward as ضارع.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r3.anchor: ومثل هذا قول الشاعر (¬4): ليبك يزيد ضارع لخصومة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r4.claim: The majority reading is preferable: رجال is the active subject of يسبح and is qualified by the phrase about trade not distracting them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r4.anchor: والوجه قراءة الجمهور، فيكون فاعل يسبح (رجال) الموصوفون (¬3) بقوله: {لا تلهيهم تجارة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r5.speaker: مقاتل، الواقدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r5.claim: Muqātil and al-Wāqidī restrict تجارة to buying, since the verse separately mentions selling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني الشراء (¬1). وبنحوه قال الواقدي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says تجارة is trade by importers, while بيع is what a man sells directly himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: التجارة لأهل الجلب، والبيع ما باعه الرجل على يديه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r7.claim: The author prefers the broad sense because تجارة includes buying and selling and is unlikely restricted to one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r7.anchor: وهذا القول أولى؛ لأن التجارة اسم للبيع والشراء فيبعد أن يخص بأحدهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r8.claim: Trade is singled out because it is the greatest and most widespread distraction from prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p293/r8.anchor: وخصت التجارة بالذكر من بين الشواغل عن الصلوات (¬4)؛ لأنها أعظم ما يشغل بها الإنسان عن الصلاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r1.speaker: المقاتلان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r1.claim: The two Muqatils take remembrance of God to mean the obligatory prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r1.anchor: قوله {عن ذكر الله} قال المقاتلان: يعني الصلوات المفروضة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r2.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ explains remembrance as attending the prescribed prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء: عن شهود الصلاة المكتوبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r3.claim: At prayer time, desire for profit does not make them delay prayer past its time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أنهم إذا حضر (¬1) وقت الصلاة لم يلههم حب الربح أن يأخروا الصلاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r4.speaker: الثوري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r4.claim: Al-Thawrī says they continued buying while attending congregational prayer in mosques.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r4.anchor: وقال الثوري: كانوا يشترون ولا يدعون الصلاة في الجماعات في المساجد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī explains إقامة الصلاة as completing the prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r5.anchor: وقوله {وإقام الصلاة} قال الكلبي: يعني: وإتمام الصلاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r6.claim: Trade does not distract them from performing prayer on time; the added phrase emphasizes establishing it at its appointed time after remembrance was already identified as prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r6.anchor: والمعنى: لا تشغلهم عن أدائها وإقامتها لوقتها (¬5). وفائدة قوله {وإقام الصلاة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives إقامة from إقواما: wāw becomes alif, one alif is deleted, and tāʾ compensates; annexation replaces the dropped tāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: يقال: أقمت الصلاة إقامة. وكان أصلها: إقواما (¬7)، ولكن قلبت الواو ألفا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ compares it to وعدته عدة and related forms, where deletion of the initial wāw leads to a compensating tāʾ; annexation allows its omission here.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r8.anchor: وزاد الفراء بيانا فقال: ومثله مما سقط بعضه فجعلت فيه الهاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r9.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r9.claim: A poetic line shortens عدة الأمر to عد الأمر, illustrating deletion of tāʾ in annexation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p295/r9.anchor: وأنشد: إن الخليط أجدوا (¬4) البين فانجردوا (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in the report through ʿAṭāʾ, says they do not withhold obligatory alms when due.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إذا حضر وقت الزكاة (¬9) لم يحبسوها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says this means the obligatory alms due on wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r2.anchor: وهو قول الحسن، قال: [يعني الزكاة الواجبة في المال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r3.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās understands zakāt as obedience to God and sincerity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال:] (¬1) يعني بالزكاة (¬2): طاعة الله والإخلاص

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r4.claim: The author prefers sincere obedience because most believers are poor and owe no financial zakāt; excluding them is unsuitable, especially since Muqātil says the verse concerned the poor ascetics of the Ṣuffa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا المعنى أنهم يبذلون من أنفسهم الطاعة الخالصة لله، ولعل الأقرب هذا؛ فإنه ليس كل المؤمنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r5.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed about the poor, ascetic people of the Ṣuffa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r5.anchor: كيف وقد قال مقاتل (¬4) في هذه الآية: نزلت في أصحاب الصفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r6.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r6.claim: Muqātil ibn Sulaymān says hearts leave the chest and lodge in throats while eyes turn blue.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r6.anchor: أحدها: أن القلوب زالت عن أماكنها من الصدور، فنشبت (¬6) في الحلوق عند الحناجر، والأبصار تزرق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r7.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the unbeliever is resurrected with sharp sight that turns blue then blind; his heart turns inside him toward the throat, seeking escape, as in 40:18.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r7.anchor: ونحوه قال الضحاك: يحشر الكافر وبصره حديد، فترزق [عيناه] (¬1)، ثم يعمى، وينقلب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r8.speaker: الفراء، الزجاج، ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r8.claim: They explain the turning as people gaining certain sight of resurrection: believers see what was promised, while unbelievers recognize its reality by heart and sight.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r8.anchor: القول الثالث: ذكره الفراء، والزجاج، وابن قتيبة. وهو: أن من كان قلبه مؤمنا بالبعث والقيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba says hearts turn from doubt and disbelief to certainty, while eyes see what had been concealed, as in Qāf 50:22.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p297/r9.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: يريد أن القلوب يوم القيامة تعرف الأمر يقينا فتنقلب عما كانت عليه من الشك والكفر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r3.claim: Hearts on Judgment Day shift between hope of salvation and fear of destruction.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r3.anchor: بين الطمع في النجاة، والحذر من الهلاك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r4.claim: People's eyes search in uncertainty about where they will be taken and from which side their book of deeds will arrive.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:36-39/r4.anchor: بين الطمع في النجاة، والحذر من الهلاك { والأبصار } تتقلب في أي ناحية

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r7.claim: Trade refers to the supplier, while sale refers to the person who sells goods with his own hands.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r7.anchor: التجارة، الجالب، والبيع الذي يبيع على يديه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r8.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddi identifies remembrance of God here as the five daily prayers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r8.anchor: قال السدي: يعني عن الصلوات الخمس.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r9.claim: When they heard the call to prayer, the men left their commerce and stood to pray; remembrance here includes the call and the five prayers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r9.anchor: كانوا إذا سمعوا المؤذن تركوا بيعهم وقاموا إلى الصلاة. وذكر الله في هذا الموضع الأذان والصلاة، والصلوات الخمس.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r10.claim: The zakah mentioned is the obligatory alms.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r11.speaker: إبراهيم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r11.claim: Ibrahim describes the named people as those whom trade does not distract from praying at its appointed time.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r11.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: قوم لا تلهيهم التجارة عن وقت الصلاة، وهم هؤلاء الذين سمى الله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r12.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r12.claim: A report says that after seeing a woman in the mosque, the Prophet told people to keep their women back, citing the punishment of the Israelites when their women went to mosques and markets.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r12.anchor: أن رسول الله رأى امرأة في المسجد فقال: «يأيها الناس كفوا عليكم نساءكم فإنما عذبت بنو إسرائيل حين أرسلوا نساءهم إلى المساجد والأسواق»

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r13.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r13.claim: Ibn Masud says a woman's best place to pray is the innermost part of her home, except for the Sacred Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque; Hamad glosses the footwear mentioned as leather socks.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r13.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: ما صلت امرأة في مكان خير من قعر بيتها، إلا أن يكون المسجد الحرام ومسجد النبي، إلا أن تخرج في منقليها. قال حماد: المنقلان: الخفان.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r14.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r14.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r14.claim: Umm Humayd al-Sa'idiya reports the Prophet's ranking: a woman's prayer at home is better than in her room, her room better than her house, her house better than the community mosque, and that mosque better than his mosque.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p450#2/r14.anchor: عن أم حميد الساعدية أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «صلاة المرأة في بيتها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r1.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r1.claim: The Prophet's report continues that a woman's prayer at her community mosque is better than at his mosque.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r1.anchor: ومسجد عشيرتها خير لها من مسجدي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r2.speaker: كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r2.claim: Ka'b says a woman's prayer at home is better than in the covered porch, and prayer in the porch is better than in her room; Qatadah adds that whatever conceals a woman is better for her.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r2.anchor: عن قتادة أن كعبا قال: صلاة المرأة في بيتها أفضل من صلاتها في صفتها وصلاتها في صفتها أفضل من صلاتها في حجرتها. ثم يتبعه قتادة: وما ستر امرأة فهو خير لها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r3.claim: Yahya gives two ways to construe the phrase: stop at “evenings” and begin a separate statement, “in the mosque are men,” or connect “men” as those who glorify God there morning and evening.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r3.anchor: وهذا الحرف يقرأ على وجهين: {يسبح له فيها} [النور: 36] في المسجد {رجال} [النور: 37]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r4.claim: The hearts and eyes that turn on that day are those of the disbelievers.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r5.claim: Their hearts are pulled from their places and lodge in their throats, unable either to return or to come out, as in 40:18.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r5.anchor: أن القلوب انتزعت من أماكنها، فغصت به الحناجر، فلا هي ترجع إلى أماكنها ولا هي تخرج

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r6.claim: The eyes' turning means they become blue after having been darkened with kohl, and blindness follows sight.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p452/r6.anchor: وأما تقلب الأبصار، فالزرق بعد الكحل، والعمى بعد البصر.

ELMALILI:24:36-38/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r4.claim: For these men, neither commerce nor buying and selling distracts them from remembering God, prayer, or giving zakat.
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r4.anchor: ne bir ticaret, ne de bir bey‘-ne alım ne satım- Allah’ı zikirden ve namaz kılmaktan ve zekât vermekten onları alıkoymaz

ELMALILI:24:36-38/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r5.claim: They fear the Day on which hearts and eyes will turn about.
ELMALILI:24:36-38/r5.anchor: kalblerin ve gözlerin döneceği günden korkarlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r6.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r6.claim: The Prophet says that a group gathering in a house of God to recite and study the Book receives tranquility and mercy, and God mentions them among those near Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r6.anchor: Bir topluluk, Allah’ın evlerinden birinde bir araya gelip Allah’ın kitabını okudukları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r10.claim: “Men” in verse 37 includes women: the masculine plural may apply generically by taġlīb or describe the usual practice; 33:35 explicitly praises worshipping men and women together.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r10.anchor: başka âyetlerde Allah’a çeşitli şekillerde ibadet edenler, bu arada O’nu zikredenler övülürken, onlara çeşitli ödüller verileceği müjdelenirken erkeklerle birlikte kadınlar da açıkça zikredilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r11.claim: Many people forget God amid trade, craft, and pleasure, neglect timely prayer, and withhold or underpay zakat, thereby failing the test of worldly wealth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r11.anchor: ticarete, zanaata, zevk ve safaya dalarak Allah’ı unuturlar, namazları vaktinde kılmazlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r12.claim: God praises servants who balance this world and the afterlife and do not trade the eternal, enduring, and valuable for what is transient; He rewards them greatly and gives beyond measure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r12.anchor: dünya-âhiret dengesini iyi kuranlar, ebedîyi fâniye, devamlıyı geçiciye, değerliyi değersize değişmeyenlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r13.speaker: Mutasavvıflar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r13.claim: Sufis cite the verse for fanāʾ: those annihilated in God retain worldly awareness without letting it veil their constant God-focused awareness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:36/r13.anchor: Mutasavvıflar bu âyetten “fenâ” dedikleri hal için bir delil çıkartmışlar

NAHHAS:v3p139/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p139/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p139/r3.claim: إقامة derives from إقوامة: the wāw’s vowel shifts to qāf, the resulting adjacent alifs lose one, and tāʾ is retained to avoid excessive deletion. In annexation, the following noun replaces tāʾ, allowing its omission.
NAHHAS:v3p139/r3.anchor: ويقال أقام الصلاة إقامة والأصل إقوامة فقلبت حركة الواو على القاف فانقلبت الواو ألفا وبعدها ألف

NAHHAS:v3p139/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p139/r4.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p139/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites poetry with عد for عدة, showing that tāʾ can drop in annexation; without annexation, وعدة keeps it.
NAHHAS:v3p139/r4.anchor:
وأنشد الفراء
( إن الخليط أجدوا البينين فانجردوا … وأخلفوك عد الأمر الذي وعدوا ) يريد عدة فحذف الهاء لما أضاف

NAHHAS:v3p139/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p139/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p139/r5.claim: One interpretation says the hearts of the wicked turn over in the Fire.
NAHHAS:v3p139/r5.anchor: قد ذكرناه وقيل معناه تتقلب قلوب الفجار على النار وقيل تتقلب

NAHHAS:v3p139/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p139/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p139/r6.claim: Another explanation is that hearts are roasted once and then scorched by the Fire another time.
NAHHAS:v3p139/r6.anchor: وقيل تتقلب أي تنضج مرة وتلفحها النار مرة

RUMMANI:v1p99#2/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p99#2/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p99#2/r1.claim: Rummani defines rhetorical homogeneity as related expressions sharing a linguistic root, and divides it into paired wording and semantic correspondence.
RUMMANI:v1p99#2/r1.anchor: تجانس البلاغة هو بيان بأنواع الكلام الذي يجمعه أصل واحد في اللغة والتجانس على وجهين

RUMMANI:v1p99#2/r5.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p99#2/r5.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p99#2/r5.claim: The paired root of turning suits both hearts, which move among thoughts, and eyes, which move among sights; both express movement or change.
RUMMANI:v1p99#2/r5.anchor: فالقلوب تتقلب بالخواطر , والأبصار تتقلب في المناظر

BURHAN:v1p50/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p50/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p50/r7.claim: Alternatively, في بيوت begins independently, and رجال is its predicate.
BURHAN:v1p50/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون منقطعا خبراا لقوله و ﴿ رجال لا تلهيهم ﴾

BURHAN:v2p501/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p501/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p501/r3.claim: After a long stretch of intervening words, repeating the explicit noun keeps the hearer's attention from being occupied with resolving a pronoun; it is also apt at a new verse opening.
BURHAN:v2p501/r3.anchor: واعلم أنه متى طال الكلام حسن إيقاع الظاهر موضع المضمر كيلا يبقى الذهن متشاغلا

BURHAN:v3p451/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p451/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p451/r3.claim: A related figure groups words sharing a linguistic root or origin; the author illustrates it with the cited Qur’anic pairings and phrases.
BURHAN:v3p451/r3.anchor: الثاني يقرب منه الاقتضاب وهو أن تكون الكلمات يجمعها أصل واحد في اللغة

ITQAN:v2p575#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r5.speaker: عبد القاهر
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r5.claim: Abd al-Qahir says explicit questions are usually answered with the noun alone, while implicit questions usually state the verb because context signals them less clearly.
ITQAN:v2p575#3/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ عبد القاهر حيث كان السؤال ملفوظا به فالأكثر ترك الفعل في الجواب والاقتصار على الاسم وحده وحيث كان مضمرا فالأكثر التصريح به

DAMGHANI:v1p191/r27.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r27.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r27.claim: The men who are not distracted by trade are those who maintain the five prayers at their appointed times.
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r27.anchor: " رجال لا تلهيهم تجار ولا بيع عن ذكر الله "

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p198/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p198/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p198/r4.claim: On Judgment Day hearts know God’s reality with certainty and leave former doubt and disbelief, while eyes see what had been veiled; compare the unveiling in 50:22.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p198/r4.anchor: يريد أن القلوب يوم القيامة تعرف أمره يقينا فتتقلب عما كانت عليه من الشك والكفر
